The State Department has notified Congress that it plans to close five U.S. diplomatic missions overseas, marking a rare reduction in America's global diplomatic footprint.

According to people familiar with the notice sent to congressional committees late last week, the closures would affect U.S. posts in St. George's, Grenada; Nagoya, Japan; Medan, Indonesia; Douala, Cameroon; and Winnipeg, Canada. The people spoke on condition of anonymity because the notification has not been made public.

The move revives an effort first pursued during the Trump administration, when officials considered closing nearly a dozen diplomatic missions as part of a broader push to reshape the federal government under an "America First" agenda.

open image in gallery Secretary of State Marco Rubio attends a Cabinet meeting hosted by President Donald Trump at Camp David in Maryland, on July 31 ( AFP/Getty )

The White House Office of Management and Budget had previously pushed for even deeper cuts, reportedly targeting as many as 30 overseas posts.

Supporters of the plan argue smaller diplomatic missions are costly and no longer essential, while critics warn the closures could weaken U.S. influence abroad.

Democrats and former foreign policy and national security officials have argued that shrinking America's diplomatic presence, combined with the dismantling of the U.S. Agency for International Development, risks leaving openings for rivals such as China and Russia to expand their influence.

open image in gallery A U.S. Consulate in Toronto was struck by gunfire in July of this year ( Reuters )

Although the State Department underwent a major reorganization last year that eliminated dozens of bureaus and hundreds of positions, no overseas missions were closed during that overhaul.

Asked about the reported closures, the State Department did not confirm the plans but said it is committed to ensuring the U.S. diplomatic network remains "efficient and effective" while following congressional notification requirements.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio has defended the administration's cost-cutting efforts, saying they are needed to "right-size" an agency that many conservatives view as overly large and bureaucratic.

open image in gallery During the administration ⁠of former ​President Joe Biden, the U.S. government opened several foreign missions, all of ​them in the Pacific region ( Getty )

The mission in St. George's is a U.S. embassy. The facilities in Nagoya, Medan and Winnipeg are consulates, while the office in Douala is an embassy branch office. Consulates and branch offices typically represent U.S. interests outside a country's capital, where the main embassy is located.

During President Joe Biden's administration, the United States expanded its diplomatic presence in the Pacific by opening several new missions as Washington sought to counter China's growing influence in the region.

China maintains diplomatic missions in St. George's, Nagoya and Medan, but does not have a diplomatic presence in Douala or Winnipeg.

Renowned horse trainer Monty Roberts has died at his farm in Solvang, California. He was 91.

Roberts was known the world over for his nonviolent method of training and his ‘join-up’ technique, which uses gestures and eye contact to gain a horse’s trust in under an hour.

His daughter, Debbie Roberts Loucks, announced his death in a social media post.

She told the New York Times that the cause was complications from an autoimmune disease.

Roberts began riding as a small child and quickly became a Hollywood stunt double, standing in for the likes of Mickey Rooney and Charlton Heston.

He started to develop his training method after watching his father, who was also a horse trainer, use a conventional fear-based approach to breaking a horse.

open image in gallery Monty Roberts on horseback at Flag is Up farm ( AFP/Getty )

He went on to study animal science at California Polytechnic State University and in 1966 founded Flag Is Up Farms in Solvang.

In 1989, the late Queen Elizabeth II – an avid horsewoman – asked Roberts to come to the UK to demonstrate his training method to her stable staff.

The pair became firm friends, and the Queen urged Roberts to write a book about his method, which was published in 1996 as The Man Who Listens to Horses.

The pair remained in contact for the rest of Elizabeth’s life, and in 2011 she appointed him an Honorary Member of the Royal Victorian Order for “services to Her Majesty’s racing establishment”.

open image in gallery Monty Roberts encourages a horse to run off its fear ( AFP/Getty )

He attended her funeral in 2022, and in 2023, a documentary named The Cowboy and the Queen was released, detailing their friendship.

Roberts said that the Queen “completely changed my life”.

His daughter, Roberts Loucks, wrote that she was announcing his death with “profound sadness”.

She went on: “For the world, he was known as the man who listens to horses. To me, he was simply Dad, a man of extraordinary kindness, unwavering integrity, and an unshakable belief that trust could accomplish what force never could.

“While our hearts are broken, we also find comfort in knowing that his legacy lives on every time someone chooses compassion over force, listens before asking, and seeks a better partnership with their horse.”

Thomas Rutter has gardened in many locations, from glorious private estates in Tuscany, to iconic gardens closer to home including Sissinghurst, Lowther Castle and Iford Manor.

When not at work, he lovingly tends his 5m x 1m balcony garden on the fourth floor of a block of flats in inner city Tottenham and is proof of the pudding that gardeners with small outside spaces can all do their bit for biodiversity.

“Any small space, whether it’s a window ledge or a crack in the wall or a balcony, or something larger like a small terrace, all have value,” says Rutter, 35, whose latest book, The Ethical Gardener, demonstrates how we can help biodiversity in large and small spaces.

“I have a small number of pots on some saucers which are full of water. I can’t tell you the number of birds that have visited my balcony in the last week for water.

“It’s very industrial where I am and the number of hoverflies and insects that are passing through, even with just a small handful of pots on a very small balcony in Tottenham, is quite remarkable.”

His top suggestions for helping biodiversity in small gardens include:

Choose suitable plants for small spaces

open image in gallery Flowering fennel (Alamy/PA)

This year, plants which have thrived on his balcony, which is south facing but in a wind tunnel, include two varieties of fennel which have been covered in pretty yellow flowers.

“Pollinators love them, but they have moved gently with the wind and because they have a filigree leaf they haven’t been too affected by the heatwave.”

Other winners have included micro agastache, species pelargoniums and Verbena bonariensis, which can move in the wind and are not so far removed from prairie plants.

open image in gallery Verbena bonariensis (Alamy/PA)

“Achillea has done quite well, which you sometimes see on the side of the road or in meadows, but actually in a pot that has done remarkably well, and a few salvias.”

Rudbeckias in pots lengthen the season, flowering later on in summer and hopefully into autumn.

“It’s important to have things that flower a little earlier, in May and June, like the salvia, then thinking about what could flower in August, September and October,” he advises.

Consider evergreens

They might not be as showy or colourful as other plants, but they do have worth for biodiversity, he points out.

“If you thought about growing ivy vertically, trailing it across the end of a balcony or covering a wall, you only need one pot to do that. And ivy has wonderful food for pollinators in autumn, but also habitat, sheltering insects over the winter, or nesting birds in spring.”

Think about one tree

A large pot should be able to accommodate a tree, he offers.

“It’s great because it provides a structure and a bit of shade, which can protect younger plants underneath it as well when the summer gets quite challenging.

“If you’re thinking about spring blossom, there’s nothing that will benefit those early-to-rise pollinators more. It might be a crab apple or a cherry tree, and you’ll find masses of pollinators around them in early spring.”

Other good candidates for pots include amelanchiers, which don’t mind a bit of shade and produce pretty blossom and can easily be kept in check, while elaeagnus or arbutus also bear fruits as well as blossom.

Create interest with underplanting

open image in gallery A small trained tree with underplanted tulips (Alamy/PA)

Underplant an evergreen tree with colourful annuals thinking about what will fill that gap for about three months.“They’re not going to last longer than a few months and you have your colour and joy, but when they are done, the tree is still there,” he says.

Alternatively, you could choose bulbs.

Try to add water

Obviously you’ll have to be careful if you are thinking about water on a balcony because of weight restrictions and drainage issues, which you’ll need to check with your landlord or management company.

open image in gallery (Alamy/PA)

“But even if it’s a small birdbath or a saucer under your pot which is taking the excess from watering, it’s surprising which birds will find a balcony to get a drink,” he says.

Leave a messy corner

If you have space such as a small terrace with a few metres, leave a small messy corner, for instance a few pots that have gone a bit wild or a shrub that you don’t cut back, which will provide sheltering spots for wildlife.

Become a beacon for wildlife

Cascade trailing plants over your balcony using window boxes which just slot on to the edge of your railings, he suggests. Even if you are a few floors up, pollinators will find them. But check with your management that you have permission to do that.

open image in gallery (Pavilion/PA)

The Ethical Gardener by Thomas Rutter is published by Pavilion on August 13, priced £16.99.

It’s meant to be one of travel’s tender moments – a last hug, a lingering wave – but readers say the UK’s airports are pricing the emotional goodbye out of existence.

Independent readers reacted with fury after analysis from the RAC found drop-off fees at Britain’s busiest airports have risen by a third on average since last summer, with a “farewell fee” at some terminals now costing more per minute than a black cab.

Many readers pointed out that kiss-and-fly zones, dedicated terminal-side drop-off and pick-up lanes at airports designed for very quick passenger transfers, are free or far cheaper in Brussels, Spain and Paris, and questioned why the UK is virtually alone among major economies in charging for the privilege of dropping someone off.

Others called for the government to cap the charges outright, while several said the fees hit hardest the people who most need to pull up at the door – those with mobility issues, heavy luggage or young children – after finding the “free” alternatives isolated, unsafe or a long way from the terminal.

Here’s what you had to say:

A stealth tax dressed up as a fee

Airport drop-off charges are exploitative and just plain ‘wrong’.

Morally wrong, because they are a stealth tax on a basic necessity. People with heavy luggage, mobility issues or young children often need a private car drop-off right at the door.

Economically wrong – passengers already pay Air Passenger Duty, and airport development fees are often embedded in ticket prices. Adding a separate charge for the kerbside means being taxed twice to access a public transport hub.

Practically wrong – airports often have aggressive enforcement (camera fines, no-stopping zones), but that just shifts the problem rather than solving it, causing congestion and risking accidents.

Environmentally wrong – public transport often isn’t viable at flight times, so the charge doesn’t change behaviour. It just extracts money from the traveller.

LittleSister

Fined for a fee I never incurred

I think it’s morally wrong and just plain fleecing the public, to be honest – actually quite extortionate. I had to drop a rental car off a few years ago and missed the turn-off, so the only route back to the slip lane was through the drop-off zone. I didn’t even drop anybody off – I simply passed through. A month later I got a fine in the post. I explained the situation and they refused to budge; they said I’d better pay or I’d get a summons.

Phasmax

British airports stink of capitalism

Free here in Spain for the first 15 minutes. British airports stink of capitalism. Bristol airport is the worst – £2 for a luggage trolley that everywhere else gives you for free, and £10 to drop someone off.

Bishop

The rot of rotten Little Britain

I used to live on a direct bus route to Heathrow, and the journey took 70 minutes with no provision for luggage on the service. A taxi took 15 minutes. For Gatwick, it was a mile’s walk to the railway station, two trains, and then arrival at the airport. The other ‘London’ airports weren’t worth considering.

Airport drop-off charges are a symptom of the rot of rotten Little Britain. Exploit all to maximum profit wherever you can is the way it works.

Every passenger has already paid (heavily) for the ‘use’ of the airport as part of the price of their ticket, and yet they have to pay more to actually get there.

Airports, like many businesses (the water industry), have lost sight of what they are there for, which is to provide a service to their customers – instead they exist purely to generate profit and pay dividends to shareholders and obscene bonuses to those already on excessive salaries.

Can Burnham stop the rot?

rEUjoin

Plan ahead and say goodbye at home

I find it more understandable for people to get upset about this somewhere like Belfast, where public transport to the airport isn’t as good as elsewhere. London airports I’ve never had a problem with (Gatwick aside). A little forward planning is all – why drive? It’s not as if you can take your car on the plane anyway. Say your goodbyes at home, take the train or bus, and save money.

PadraigMahone

Charged for a delay that wasn't my fault

I had to pay a heavy charge when picking up a relative at Newcastle airport: the plane was late but no one seemed to know why (it was delayed two hours at Bristol). As no one knew when the plane would arrive, I couldn’t go away and come back later. This is a rip-off.

Suney

A different perspective

Here’s a different perspective. Travel is an expensive hassle from the moment of decision till the moment of return. The internet now allows you to find out about most costs in advance. If you need to take a car to the pay-for drop-off zone, find out about it beforehand. Buy one less new garment for your holiday and drink one less unit of alcohol a day during it. And don’t perform a movie farewell in public if possible: either your relationship is strong or it isn’t. Stay safe.

totallytottingham

Liverpool's a fiver just to drop and go

I may have missed it, but Liverpool is one of the worst. It’s a fiver to drive into their drop-off, kick out and then drive straight out. And that’s on top of £2 each way over the Mersey Flow.

AGS

Paris does it better

Drop-off charges at Paris airports (Charles de Gaulle and Orly) are free for the first ten minutes in designated express zones, followed by steep penalty fees if you stay longer.

Hairyferrit

Unlawful and exploitative

I am glad someone wrote about it. These drop-off charges are unlawful and exploitative. Airports charge people who don’t even take a flight or use their loo. And these prices keep going up and up, and it looks like no one controls those hikes.

Lukas

No alternative if you live outside a city

Living in East Anglia, driving isn’t a choice, it’s a necessity; the privatised public transport is unreliable and expensive. For two of us, it’s cheaper and three hours quicker to drive to Luton and stay overnight, with parking and breakfast, than two return train tickets – and that includes getting to Stansted as well. Plus with flight delays and train cancellations, it’s a genuinely risky option – might be fine for people in London or Manchester, but not where I live.

Nicko

The 'free' option isn't safe after dark

At my local airport, the only free drop-off point is – and has been for a long time – the medium-stay car park. It’s no great distance from the terminal building, but it’s along a short, isolated and overgrown footpath – not great for female passengers on their own, and especially not for those of us arriving in the dark for an early flight.

Tanaquil2

Burnham should turn his fire on this too

Good this has been raised. Burnham is criticising lots of things, and these need it too. Forget the romantic side – it’s the exploitative impossibility of it. You do have the option to leave passengers at the usual car parks to catch the free bus service, and park free for 20 minutes, but this can be remote from the airport terminus. Just bring back the free drop-off facility, which was largely respected.

Luckybeeme

A Covid-era charge that never came down

I seem to recall the Heathrow drop-off charge was introduced to help the recovery after Covid – it was recently put up. They are now saying charges to passengers will go up to cover the airport expansion – in what universe do new projects get added to old businesses? How about the expansion funds itself, and private companies actually take a risk for a change?

ProBonoComments

Americans now trust Democrats more than Republicans to handle the economy for the first time in nearly a decade, according to a new Reuters/Ipsos poll that also found President Donald Trump's approval rating has slipped to 35%.

The survey, conducted from Wednesday through Monday, suggests Trump's handling of the economy could become a major issue heading into November's midterm elections, when control of Congress will be at stake.

Trump's approval rating fell from 37% in last month's Reuters/Ipsos poll to 35%, just one point above the lowest level of his current term.

open image in gallery The finding, in a poll conducted Wednesday through Monday, showed how Trump's handling of the economy, including rising energy prices resulting from the Iran war, could weigh on his party's chances in the November midterm elections ( Reuters )

Asked which party would do a better job managing the economy, 37% of registered voters chose Democrats, compared with 36% who backed Republicans. Another 27% said they were unsure or preferred another party.

Republicans had held the advantage on the economy through most of Trump's first term, President Joe Biden's presidency and the early months of Trump's current term. While a Reuters/Ipsos poll in 2017 also showed Democrats ahead, that survey used different wording and did not include an "unsure" option.

The GOP's long-standing edge has steadily narrowed during Trump's second term as Americans grapple with higher living costs, including a sharp rise in gasoline prices following the U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in February and the continuing conflict.

open image in gallery Some 37% of registered voters responding to the poll said the Democratic Party has a better approach to ​the U.S. economy, compared with 36% who picked the Republican Party ( Getty )

Trump has said the strikes were intended to dismantle Iran's nuclear program, curb its regional influence and create conditions for regime change. Since the conflict began, gasoline prices have risen by more than 25%, with drivers paying more than $1 extra per gallon.

The poll also found Democrats leading the generic congressional ballot, with 42% of registered voters saying they would back a Democratic candidate if elections were held today, compared with 37% for a Republican. Independent voters favored Democrats by a 12-point margin.

Republicans are defending narrow majorities in both chambers of Congress, though only about three dozen House races and roughly eight Senate contests are expected to be highly competitive.

open image in gallery The ​Republican edge on the economy has steadily deteriorated during Trump's current term, narrowing to zero in recent months ( Copyright 2022 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

Trump has repeatedly rejected polls showing declining public support. Before the Reuters/Ipsos survey was released, he wrote on Truth Social: "My REAL Polling Numbers, not those made up by the Fake News Media, are the best they have ever been."

The Reuters/Ipsos online poll surveyed 4,505 U.S. adults and has a margin of error of plus or minus 2 percentage points.

Former MasterChef judge Marco Pierre White isn’t exactly known for mincing his words – and he’s now given a no-holds-barred verdict on the popular cookery series, telling fans: “Don’t take it seriously.”

The 64-year-old has made numerous MasterChef appearances over the years, serving as a principal judge and co-host on multiple series of Australia’s MasterChef: The Professionals and popping up on the South Africa and New Zealand versions of the show.

In 2024, he appeared as a guest judge in the grand final of the BBC’s MasterChef. But White’s latest comments suggest he perhaps won’t be rushing back to the studios.

Describing MasterChef as “a reality show”, he told the Daily Mirror: “When it comes to the tasting the food is three, four hours old. It's cold food.

“It is a TV show, don't take it seriously. It is not real. It is fantasy. If it makes you want to cook then that is all that matters. It’s food porn."

open image in gallery Marco Pierre White ( PA )

White first worked as a chef in Harrogate before moving to London in the early 1980s, where he began classical training under the tutelage of Albert and Michel Roux at the highly-esteemed Le Gavroche.

By the late 1980s, White was overseeing his own establishments and in 1995, he became the youngest chef to receive three Michelin stars – which he famously handed back when he quit daily kitchen work in 1999.

The star then turned his attention to investing as a restaurateur and making a name for himself as a celebrity and television chef.

MasterChef has occasionally proven to be the perfect springboard for home cooks who have gone on to have hugely successful careers in the food industry.

Thomasina Miers won the series in 2005, before going on to found the hugely popular restaurant chain Wahaca, and Dean Edwards - now resident chef on ITV’s Lorraine - was a runner-up the following year.

More recently, MasterChef has had a tumultuous couple of years.

open image in gallery Torode and Wallace departed the show last year ( BBC/Shine TV )

In November 2024, it was announced that longtime host Gregg Wallace would temporarily step away from the show amid allegations of inappropriate behaviour and sexual misconduct.

In July 2025, an independent review commissioned by MasterChef’s production company upheld 43 of the 85 allegations and Wallace’s permanent departure was announced.

The majority of the upheld claims related to inappropriate sexual language, or culturally insensitive or racist remarks. The presenter said in a statement at the time that "none of the serious allegations against me were upheld”.

He added: "I challenged the remaining issue of unwanted touching but have had to accept a difference in perception, and I am deeply sorry for any distress caused. It was never intended."

open image in gallery MasterChef’s new hosts ( BBC/Shine TV )

In the same month, it was announced that his co-host John Torode had been dismissed for historic “racist remarks”.

Torode said he had “absolutely no recollection of any of this and I do not believe that it happened”, but added: "However, I want to be clear that I've always had the view that any racial language is wholly unacceptable in any environment.

“I'm shocked and saddened by the allegation as I would never wish to cause anyone any offence."

MasterChef is now hosted by food critic Grace Dent and Irish chef Anna Haugh.

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
“It means everything – absolutely incredible,” said Kerr, who joined the rendition of Flower of Scotland before closing his eyes to soak up the moment in a stadium where he had competed as a child in even the shot put.

“To do it in front of a Scottish crowd, where I learned how to race, doesn’t get any better,” he added. “I came here week after week growing up as a kid. This was the championship of my season with the world indoors and going after the record. This was on the calendar before any of that. I think a British crowd deserved more from me and I owed them that.”

Of the tactics compared to his world record, where he had to hold an even pace throughout, Kerr stressed the importance of staying calm and not being tempted into pushing too soon. “London was a big stress, pushing my body to the extreme limit,” he said. “Doing a championship race is a nice clean slate; using your brain instead of your body. It’s how I love to race.

“When you’re running that slow, your job is not to waste energy and I did that. I knew an opportunity would open up. Then it was about staying awake and alive and trying to get some space. felt like I had plenty of gears left in me.”

Kerr had emerged to a huge home ovation and, with the Proclaimers booming out as the runners completed the first two laps, he was content to stay in the pack even as Myers followed. There was then only one brief moment of concern as the runners began gathering themselves during the penultimate lap and Kerr became momentarily boxed in.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

Sports.title: Forgotten former Arsenal keeper, 38, keeps clean sheet in Carabao Cup clash 18 months after his last appearance
Sports.content:
FORMER Arsenal goalkeeper Vito Mannone kept a clean sheet on his debut as player coach with Crawley in the Carabao Cup.

Mannone, 38, joined the League Two outfit in June having played his last competitive match with former club Lille in February 2025.



The ex-Italy youth international took charge of the EFL side’s goalkeeping department while being available for selection two months ago.

And the ex-Arsenal shot stopper made his bow between the sticks in the Carabao Cup.



Crawley visited York City in the preliminary round on Monday at York Community Stadium.

And Mannone enjoyed a successful debut as he kept a clean sheet by helping another former Arsenal ace in Colin Kazim-Richards – now manager of the club – pick up a 2-0 win.



The Red Devils broke the deadlock on 24 minutes thanks to Gianmarco Di Biasse’s opener.

And Danilo Orsi sealed the big away win from the penalty spot four minutes before full-time.

Crawley are now set to visit Watford on Saturday in the Carabao Cup’s first round.

Mannone joined Arsenal from Atalanta in 2005 and underwent a loan stint at Barnsley a year later before making his competitive debut with the first team in 2009.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Italian also spent two seasons on loan at Hull between 2010 and 2012 before returning to the Emirates where he amassed a total of 23 appearances throughout an eight-year period.

Mannone left the Gunners in 2013 and underwent quite the nomadic career in England and abroad.

That included stints with Sunderland, Reading, Minnesota United, Esbjerg, Monaco, Lorient and Lille.

Sports.title: Champions League stadium to look unrecognisable as £171m renovation of 54,732-seater arena is approved
Sports.content:
NAPOLI are set to give the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona a mega-money makeover.

The Serie A giants, who are eyeing a summer move for Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile, have had major redevelopment plans approved.



It comes after Chelsea fans highlighted safety issues when they headed to Napoli in the Champions League last season.

And the Italian heavyweights’ 54,732-seater home will look unrecognisable after the £171million renovation is complete.



The athletics track separating the action from the raucous fans is set to be ditched as part of the proposal.

Napoli, who bagged their fourth Serie A crown last year, also want to extend the second tier and have the seating just seven metres from the edge of the pitch.



The third tier will also be reopened after being off limits to supporters due to safety concerns.

Structural vibrations could be felt when fans were celebrating, leading to changes needing to be made.

But having fans back in those areas could allow the capacity at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona – which was renamed in honour of the Argentine legend in 2020 – to increase to in the region of 65,000.

Initial preparatory work has already begun and is expected to move into a more advanced stage in the autumn.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But Napoli, fresh from seeing Antonio Conte quit as their boss at the end of last term, are desperate not to stray too far from how the arena looked when it first opened in 1959.

The eye-catching renovation, which includes new VIP boxes and hospitality areas, is on course to take place in stages.

It means Napoli, who are preparing for another season of Champions League action, will not have to leave their home while upgrades are made.

And the project was given the green light after a proposal was submitted by Mayor Gaetano Manfredi and infrastructure councillor Edoardo Cosenza.



The majority of the building work is expected to get underway after Italian host cities for Euro 2032 have been selected.

But city and regional authorities insist Stadio Diego Armando Maradona will be revamped even if it is not in line to stage showdowns during the tournament.

Sports.title: Leeds boss Daniel Farke fumes as team are denied trophy after pre-season win over Liverpool
Sports.content:
DANIEL FARKE was left miffed that Leeds’ pre-season victory over Liverpool did not come with a trophy.

The Yorkshire club rounded off their US tour with a 4-2 win over the Reds in Chicago thanks to an excellent second-half comeback.



It made it two wins from three games after beating Sunderland and losing to Wrexham in the round-robin tournament.

A Dominic Calvert-Lewin double, plus goals from Brenden Aaronson and Sean Longstaff did the damage.



It meant Leeds finished as the top British club — but did not receive any silverware for their efforts.

And boss Farke said: “We won this tournament and actually I want the trophy.



Especially in the US, you normally get the trophy for everything!

“I am a bit annoyed, but all jokes aside, there couldn’t be a better ending of this tour.

“The boys have worked so hard — three weeks right now without a day off, more or less two weeks here in the US.

“Against Liverpool, we had more shots, more shots on target, way more corner kicks, set-pieces.

“We really fully deserved to win this game.

“Especially for such a brilliant, brilliant second half — so all credit goes to the players.

“We take lots of positives, not just from this game but lots of positives out of this tour.

“We will head back to the UK, need then perhaps one or two days to recover, then we go again.”



The Whites host German club RB Leipzig in their next pre-season friendly on Saturday.

Meanwhile, Liverpool’s pre-season was looking fairly positive – until the Leeds bump in the road – with two wins over Sunderland and Wrexham.

Their transfer window has occupied fewer headlines than last summer despite talisman Mo Salah’s exit.

Sports.title: Why Jude Bellingham nemesis Valentin Barco won’t care less if he gets booed at Premier League grounds with Chelsea
Sports.content:
ARGENTINIAN hothead Valentin Barco can expect a hostile reception from English fans whenever he plays for Chelsea this season.

But the red-haired firebrand who earned a clip round the ear from Jude Bellingham for his World Cup semi-final antics is no stranger to bouncing back from controversy.



Barco, 22, may have compatriot and fellow wind-up merchant Enzo Fernandez to help him run the gauntlet.

No-one has yet stumped up the £120m fee which Chelsea are demanding for Fernandez, who cupped his ears in front of Three Lions fans as he celebrated his equaliser against Thomas Tuchel’s men.



Yet whatever happens with his international team-mate, Barco will surely face the consequences of his behaviour following Lautaro Martinez’s stoppage-time winner.

The former Brighton star, who was an unused substitute, ran on to the pitch and appeared to taunt England players.

And after the final whistle, Barco said or did something to antagonise Bellingham further, which resulted in the slap for which the Three Lions star has escaped punishment.

Venezuela’s Bryant Ortega was not so lucky when Barco was up to no good in an Olympic qualifying match back in February 2024.



After Barco was penalised for a foul, he threw the ball at another opponent, Rafael Uzcategui, catching him on the head.

Ortega retaliated on behalf of his team-mate in similar fashion, and both he and Barco were sent off.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Argentina feared Barco would be banned for the remaining two matches of the final stage of qualifying..

But Barco received just a one-game ban and returned for the decisive game against Brazil.

Playing at left back, he secured his third assist of the campaign by setting up what turned out to be the only goal of the game, which sent Argentina to the Paris 2024 games.



But for good measure, Barco showed the other side of his game in stoppage time by earning a yellow card for kicking the ball away as Brazil prepared to take a free kick.

All this happened after Barco had signed for Brighton from Boca Juniors in January 2024 for just under £8m – but before he made an appearance for the Seagulls.

The transatlantic move was not the first time Barco had gone the extra mile to advance his career.

Boca spotted his talent at an early age, but his home in Veinticinco de Mayo was a long way from the academy.

Barco revealed: “When I started playing football, my mother and then my father would travel 100km to take me to training every day.



“After that, we moved to live next to the stadium.”

Boca, where Diego Maradona and many other Argentina legends rose to fame, converted Barco from a wide forward into a left-sided defender.

He made his debut at the age of 16 and at 19 was part of the team which made it all the way to the 2023 final of the Copa Libertadores, South America’s equivalent of the Champions League.

In the last 16 clash with Uruguay’s Nacional, he stepped up to score the fifth and decisive penalty in the shootout.

Barco started the final against Brazilian side Fluminense, but Boca lost 2-1 after extra time.



Manchester City were among the clubs monitoring Barco.

But it was Brighton who announced Barco was following in the footsteps of fellow South American recruits to the Amex such as fellow Argentinian Alexis Mac Allister and Ecuador’s Moises Caicedo, now his team-mate at Chelsea.

Barco made seven appearances for Brighton in the remainder of the 2023/4 campaign, including three starts in the Premier League.



The Seagulls sent the young man on loan to Spanish club Sevilla for the 2024/5 campaign.

But he returned in the New Year after struggling for game time and with injuries. Barco and fiancee Yaz Jaureguy, an influencer from Argentina, were also victims of a burglary.

A move to Strasbourg and the coaching of future Chelsea boss Liam Rosenior kickstarted Barco’s European adventure.

After recovering from a hamstring problem, he started all 14 remaining Ligue 1 games.

Just as significantly, Rosenior unlocked his potential in a new position.



Barco initially played as a wing back for Strasbourg, but soon found himself playing in the centre of midfield alongside Andrey Santos, who was on loan from sister club Chelsea.

He thrived at the heart of the team and became a key player in the side that secured Conference League qualification.

Barco was outstanding in a 4-2 win over Lyon in March 2025 and was given three days off by Rosenior to spend with Jaureguy and their new baby daughter.



Barco joined Strasbourg permanently for £8m and continued his development, even after Rosenior left in January to replace Enzo Maresca as Chelsea boss.

The Blues were immediately linked with a move to sign him, and personal terms were allegedly agreed back In April..

Strasbourg enjoyed another good season, reaching the semi finals of the Conference League and French Cup.

The only blot on Barco’s copybook was a red card for an X-rated foul on Lens’ Morgan Guilavogui last November.

Until the World Cup semi final.



Argentinians call people with ginger hair like Barco “Colo” – short for “colorado”.

And he lived up to their reputation for being combustible with his behaviour against England, despite not kicking a ball in anger in Atlanta.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Barco can expect plenty of stick up and down the country when he pulls on a Chelsea shirt following a move which even some Blues fans are criticising.

But like any good Argentinian, he is unlikely to care.

Sports.title: West Ham chief David Sullivan advised to stay away from home matches after ‘historic sexual misconduct allegations’
Sports.content:
DAVID Sullivan, West Ham’s co-owner, has been advised to stay away from home matches following allegations of historic sexual misconduct.

The 77-year-old billionaire recently quit the football club after a BBC Panorama investigation revealed several women accused Sullivan of predatory behaviour and sexual exploitation, which he denies



The London Stadium, where West Ham play their home games, said it “recommended” Sullivan does not attend these matches, the BBC revealed.

The advice was given following concerns about “potential for demonstrations and anti-social behaviour by some spectators”.



A spokesperson for the stadium told the BBC it asked Sullivan to give advance notice if he planned to make a visit so additional safety measures could be implemented.

It said: “Following media reports at the end of the season regarding a safeguarding matter being managed by the club, London Stadium sought further information to ensure it could fulfil its own safeguarding responsibilities.”

The stadium also said that West Ham informed it that “the matter was investigated and that the club does not consider there to be an ongoing safeguarding risk associated with Mr Sullivan attending the stadium”.

Sullivan has branded the claims of serious sexual misconduct as “factually incorrect and entirely false”.



Despite this, the stadium still wanted Sullivan to stay away from home games following fan unrest.

However, it is understood that Sullivan is expected to defy these requests.

The BBC approached Sullivan for comment but he did not respond.

The Sun have approached London Stadium and West Ham for comment.

This new advice comes after a BBC Panorama and Times investigation revealed allegations against Sullivan for historical sex abuse.



He has been accused of abusing his power to prey on young women for sex – allegations dating back to the 1980s.

Women alleged he used his position as owner of the Daily and Sunday Sport to pressure aspiring models into sex and proposition others.

One woman, known as Florence, claimed she felt forced to have sex with him at his Essex mansion.

She said she made excuses – telling him her boyfriend was in the house and that she was on her period – but claims Sullivan ignored her.

Sullivan disputes her version of events and says her account of his home makes her claims implausible.



The tycoon had also been secretly banned from having contact with the club’s youth and women’s matches for three years over safeguarding fears.

A safeguarding panel made up of the club, the FA and the local authority ruled he should be kept away from the teams and was informed of the ban in writing by a senior club executive.

Sullivan, who had been on the board for more than 16 years, later resigned and vowed to sue the BBC for libel, calling the Panorama allegations made against him “defamatory”.

Following his resignation in June, a Hammers club statement read: “West Ham United can confirm that Joint-Chair David Sullivan has stepped down from his position with immediate effect.

“Mr Sullivan has also resigned as a director of both WH Holding Limited and West Ham United Football Club, having been made aware of the impending publication of serious historic allegations.



“It is understood none of the allegations relate to West Ham United or any of its operations.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Through his own legal representatives Mr Sullivan denies any illegal conduct and has taken the decision to step down in order to avoid disruption to the Club while he addresses the matter privately.

“Interim Chief Executive Officer Karim Virani, reporting into the current Board of Directors, will continue to be responsible for leading the Club’s day-to-day operations.”

Sports.title: Man Utd paying price for years of transfer failure as Marcus Rashford and £36.5m flop prove impossible to budge
Sports.content:
THE 2007 transfer window was Manchester United’s best — not just for who they bought, but also for who they sold.

It is in stark contrast to the current summer, where the Red Devils’ only senior sale agreed has been 21-year-old Tyler Fredricson.



The full-back made four appearances before moving to the Ineos-owned Lausanne Sport in Switzerland — so he barely counts.

While United’s Big Six rivals are splashing the cash, the Red Devils are paying the price for years of a sub-par approach to sales.



Arsenal, hot in the pursuit of Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Jr, are the only one of those clubs to have splashed less cash than the Old Trafford outfit.

The Red Devils have so far spent just £87million on Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, Tynan Thompson, while keeper Karl Darlow has arrived on a free.



Put simply, the more cash that United generate from outgoings, the more they can spend — and the lack of sales are hurting them.

Manchester City and Chelsea regularly lean on their network of sister clubs to trade players for profit.

That could be a homegrown academy product sold, for example, from Chelsea to Strasbourg.

Or a BlueCo-owned player going the other way before getting flipped within 18 months for a profit on the Stamford Bridge books.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Ineos also own Nice — but United have not taken advantage of that relationship, with Sir Jim Ratcliffe looking to sell the French-owned club. While hardly fetching mega sums, United’s academy still sells.

Andreas Pereira (£10m), James Garner (£15m), Dean Henderson (£20m), Anthony Elanga (£15m) and Alejandro Garnacho (£40m) all moved to Premier League rivals since 2022.

But Kobbie Mainoo and Shea Lacey are the only current first-team players produced by United’s academy.

Garnacho was the last United graduate to generate serious profit when Chelsea brought him last summer.

Nineteen years ago, United were pulling in good money for players they wanted to sell. In the same summer they signed Nani, Anderson and Owen Hargreaves.



Kieran Richardson joined Sunderland for £5.5m, while fellow academy graduate Giuseppe Rossi relocated to Villarreal permanently for £6.7m.

Alan Smith went to Newcastle for £6million and Gabriel Heinze headed to Real Madrid for £8m, having failed to engineer a move to bitter rivals Liverpool.

United were in a position of strength as reigning Prem champions.



And it helped that playing for Sir Alex Ferguson increased a player’s valuation.

Roy Keane could barely stomach sharing the same oxygen as Ferguson after United dumped him — but still signed five players from his old club as Sunderland boss.

It is incredible that Garnacho, Scott McTominay, Rasmus Hojlund, Mason Greenwood, Daniel James, David Beckham, Cristiano Ronaldo, Angel Di Maria and Romelu Lukaku are the only players United have sold for £25m or more.

The Red Devils desperately trumpeted Garnacho to Chelsea as a record academy sale at £40m.

He appeared to be sold on the cheap but Garnacho, now at Aston Villa, was so feckless that Chelsea might even have overpaid.



Out-of-favour forward Joshua Zirkzee is still on United’s books and Marcus Rashford remains in the building after a permanent move to Barcelona fell through following his loan.

It has been so long since Rashford was last back in the fold at United that he has not set foot in their new £50m building at Carrington, reopened a year ago.

It is a blow for Rashford that Villa, his ex-club who he thanked for his England World Cup 2026 call-up, opted for Garnacho, his old United left-wing challenger.

Rashford is not exactly old at 28 — but Villa and Barca moved for younger wingers.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His £325,000 weekly salary makes a sale prohibitive.



Even Richardson, a very different left winger at Old Trafford 20 years ago, was an easier sell.

Sports.title: West Ham eye transfer for forgotten Tottenham star, 27, who hasn’t played for the club in three years
Sports.content:
WEST HAM are interested in signing Tottenham forward Manor Solomon.

The Israel star, 27, is set to leave Spurs this summer and talks over an exit will ramp up this week – with Fiorentina, where he spent the second half of last season, also keen.



The Hammers are looking for reinforcements out wide following Crysencio Summerville’s exit.

Super agent Pini Zahavi is involved in talks and wants to find Solomon a new home before the season gets underway.



Fiorentina are pushing to bring the winger back after he helped the Serie A side qualify for Europe last season.

Solomon’s spell at Fiorentina in the second half of last season was his third loan spell in two years – after also spending time with Leeds and Villarreal.

He enjoyed a box office campaign at Leeds and helped Daniel Farke’s side win promotion back to the top-flight.

A return to the Prem is also an attractive option for the versatile winger, who can play on either flank.

He joined Tottenham from Fulham in 2023 but has played just SIX competitive games.

His last outing for Tottenham came back in September 2023 under Ange Postecoglou.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Despite his uncertain future, Solomon has featured regularly in pre-season, starting friendlies against MK Dons, Auckland FC, Sydney FC and Chelsea.

Only midfielder Archie Gray has clocked more minutes than the 49-cap Israel international.

But while Roberto De Zerbi has taken a long look at the winger this summer, he is still expected to leave before the transfer window shuts.

Sports.title: Managing Newcastle as new striker added and Bruno Guimaraes makes final call
Sports.content:
Managing Newcastle as new striker added and Bruno Guimaraes makes final call

Newcastle United's incoming manager Matthias Jaissle has a lot of big decisions to make in his first transfer window at the helm

View 3 Images Matthias Jaissle will have plenty on his plate at Newcastle (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

It has been a challenging summer for Newcastle United but fans will hope the appointment of new manager Matthias Jaissle leads to some more positive transfer news. Al-Ahli boss Jaissle looks poised to take over following the departure of Eddie Howe and he will have work to do.

‌



Things have moved more quickly than at this stage of last summer's window, when Anthony Elanga was the only player to arrive before the start of August. More than £130million has been spent on new signings, though there have also been high-profile exits.

‌



Ivorian winger Bazoumana Toure has joined, ostensibly as a replacement for Anthony Gordon after the England star joined Barcelona. Sandro Tonali has also left, joining Tottenham in a deal worth up to £100m, with young midfielders Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba moving to St James' Park in an effort to soften the blow.

‌



In goal, new arrivals Ewen Jaouen and Lukas Hornicek have both joined. This is expected to pave the way for Nick Pope to leave the club, while experienced heads including Kieran Trippier and Emil Krafth have already moved on.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Arsenal target Bruno Guimaraes complies with Newcastle requests as midfielder touches down READ MORE :

There are still a number of matters which need to be resolved, though, not least the future of captain Bruno Guimaraes. Here, we've taken a look at what Jaissle can do to set the Magpies on the right path for the new campaign.

‌



Add midfield experience

While Bruno Guimaraes remains at Newcastle for now and a bid has been rejected, he is expected to be an Arsenal player by the end of the window. Ideally, they will want to avoid a repeat of last year when the Alexander Isak transfer saga dragged out to the point that they arguably overpaid on both Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa.

Tonali has already gone and Joelinton could yet follow amid reports of Saudi Pro League interest. Bamba and Steur have arrived with high ceilings but trusting your midfield operations to two players under the age of 21 feels like a risk Newcastle can't afford to take.

View 3 Images Newcastle have knocked back a bid for Bruno Guimaraes (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



If two more midfielders end up joining, Croatian World Cup star Petar Sucic could end up being one of them. Reports in Italy suggest the Inter Milan talent could be available for just over £38m, though Leeds are also keen.

Another man linked with a move is former Nottingham Forest man Danilo. Sporting director Ross Wilson brought the Brazil international to England back in 2023 and now could repeat the trick in the north east, with ESPN reporting in July that he is considered a potential replacement should Guimaraes depart.

Convince Lewis Hall to stay

Newcastle might well end up fighting a losing battle on their skipper, which makes it all the more important that they come out on the right side as far as Hall is concerned. The left-back has been a revelation since joining from Chelsea but that has naturally brought interest.

‌



Manchester United's interest appears to be the most concrete, with reports of a £60m opening bid in the near future. Michael Carrick's side are said to have internally approved a move for a player who they consider a long-term successor to Luke Shaw.

View 3 Images Lewis Hall has been involved for Newcastle in pre-season (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Hall is under contract until 2029, though, so incoming boss Jaissle ought not to be under huge pressure to sell. Keeping the defender on board would send a key message going into a first season with a new man in the dugout.

‌



Replace Alexander Isak's goals

It goes without saying that goals were a problem for Newcastle in Howe's final season at the helm. Isak scored 23 in the league in his final season for the club before completing a deadline day move to Liverpool and Woltemade, Wissa and Will Osula - the three nominal strikers tasked with replacing that tally - managed just 16 between them.

Wissa was the biggest disappointment, netting just once in the league as he endured an injury-hit season following a £50m move from Brentford. The arrival of Jaissle could offer him a fresh start, though, after he showed some sharpness with a return of three goals for DR Congo at the World Cup.

It may well still be the case that a new marquee striker signing is needed, putting the Tonali and Gordon money to good use. Out-of-favour Chelsea striker Liam Delap has been linked, while Jaissle's arrival could well increase noise over a potential St James' Park return for Ivan Toney, who thrived under the German at Al-Ahli last season and earned a World Cup call-up as a result.

Article continues below

“Never say never,” Toney told Sky Sports News in February when asked about a Premier League return. “I have goals I want to achieve here first, the club have signed me for a long period of time. I want to repay them and bring trophies. In football and life, you never know what’s around the corner. Who knows what the next step is?

Sports.title: Arsenal may be using Vinicius Jr transfer talk as smokescreen for another huge deal
Sports.content:
Arsenal may be using Vinicius Jr transfer talk as smokescreen for another huge deal

Arsenal's chase of Vinicius Jr could pave the way for another marquee arrival in north London this summer

View 2 Images Vinicius Jr could be heading to the Premier League (Image: Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

Arsenal would be pulling off the biggest transfer in their history if they acquire Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid. However, their chase for the Brazilian star may not tell the full story of Mikel Arteta's transfer intentions.

‌



The Gunners' stunning interest in the 26-year-old was reported last week by The Athletic, who stated they'd be keen on signing him if he doesn't sign a new deal with the Spanish giants.

‌



Vinicius has just 12 months left on his contract and Madrid could be inclined to sell him this summer rather than let him leave for free next year. Even before the sale of Leandro Trossard to Besiktas, a marquee attacker was a priority for Arteta in his attempts to bolster their chances of defending their Premier League title this upcoming season.

‌



The Madrid superstar certainly fits the bill, but he isn't the only forward that Arsenal have had their eyes on this window. Yan Diomande has been a target for the north London outfit, with Liverpool, Paris Saint-Germain and Madrid all registering serious interest in signing the RB Leipzig left-winger.

While Vinicius is currently the superior player, Diomande, 19, is seven years younger than him and is equally adept at playing on both flanks. The Brazilian's contract situation could have played a role in Madrid moving forward in their attempts to sign the Ivorian, having launched an unsuccessful £85million bid for his services.

Vinicius Junior transfer: Arsenal ready to break salary record to sign Real Madrid star READ MORE :

Arsenal's two conditions for Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Gunners set to make next move READ MORE :

Arsenal's interest in Vinicius could be a calculated tactic to force Madrid to focus on extending his contract, which could result in the Gunners moving ahead of the pack in the race for Diomande.

‌



Talks may continue to loom over the Brazil international's future, but according to Diario AS, there is optimism that a deal can be reached to continue his eight-year tenure at the Santiago Bernabeu.

View 2 Images Yan Diomande is nearing a move to Real Madrid (Image: Hugo Rivera/Jam Media/Getty Images)

That optimism seems to have no bearing on their efforts to sign Diomande, with Sky Germany reporter Florian Plettenberg reporting that the winger has reached a 'verbal agreement' to join the La Liga side.

‌



However, the deal has hit a speed bump, with Leipzig managing director Marcel Schafer casting doubt on the progression of Diomande's move to Madrid. The German appeared to indirectly slam Fabrizio Romano for seemingly confirming Diomande's eventual sale on X.

The Italian had used his catchphrase 'Here We Go' when claiming an agreement between Leipzig and Madrid had been found in a deal worth over £85m for the Ivorian. Schafer unequivocally told Sky Germany: "It’s clear that some so-called transfer experts reported a few days ago that the deal was done or gave it the ‘here we go.’ That’s simply not the case. We’re not at that stage yet."

The update certainly gives credence to Arsenal's ability to usurp Madrid in acquiring Diomande. Just over a month remains in the transfer market and while they've added Christos Tzolis to their ranks following an impressive stint at Club Brugge, there's no doubt the opportunity to capture one of the leading attackers in world football will be a deal Arsenal chase until the window slams shut.

Sports.title: Ex-FIFA president was forced to resign and banned from football for 12 years
Sports.content:
Ex-FIFA president was forced to resign and banned from football for 12 years

Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter remains banned from the sport as his successor Gianni Infantino comes under pressure

View 2 Images Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter remains banned from football (Image: FABRICE COFFRINI/AFP via Getty Images)

Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter is still serving his ban from all football-related activities. The 90-year-old received two suspensions totalling more than 12 years, keeping him out of the sport until June 2028.

‌



In more recent times, Blatter’s successor Gianni Infantino has faced backlash after plans to sell stakes in FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors were revealed. The English Football Association is reportedly set to follow the Welsh FA in withdrawing support for Infantino’s re-election.

‌



European governing body UEFA recently said in a statement: "The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.”

‌



While Infantino faces an uncertain future at FIFA, it is not the first time that the head of football’s world governing body has caused controversy. Blatter became head of FIFA in 1998 and remained in the role before being forced to resign in June 2015 after coming under investigation by the USA as part of a corruption inquiry.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

During a press conference, Blatter said: "My mandate does not appear to be supported by everybody." He was later given an eight-year ban from football in December 2015, alongside UEFA president Michel Platini, which was ultimately reduced to six years.

‌



Gianni Infantino was set to earn huge salary from World Cup plan as staggering figure revealed READ MORE :

The suspension related to alleged ethics breaches after Blatter made a £1.3million payment to Platini in 2011. Both parties argued the money was part of a verbal agreement for the latter’s work as a technical adviser between 1998 and 2002.

Both men, who always denied wrongdoing, were subsequently cleared of corruption charges in Swiss courts in 2025 in relation to the payment.

However that came some time after Blatter had already announced his plan to step away from FIFA and allow the governing body to find his replacement, with Infantino officially becoming his successor in February 2016.

‌



Blatter received a further suspension in March 2021. He was banned from the sport for another six years and eight months, upon the end of his initial suspension in October 2021, keeping him out of football until June 2028.

It was imposed following multiple breaches of FIFA's ethics code. The same length of suspension was also imposed on FIFA's former secretary general, Jerome Valcke.

The governing body found that Blatter received "an undue economic benefit" of 23m Swiss Francs (£18m) between 2010 and 2014.

‌



View 2 Images Blatter will remain suspended from all football-related activities until June 2028 (Image: Fabrice COFFRINI / AFP via Getty Images)

A Fifa statement said: "The investigations into Messrs Blatter and Valcke covered various charges, in particular concerning bonus payments in relation to Fifa competitions that were paid to top Fifa management officials, various amendments and extensions of employment contracts, as well as reimbursement by Fifa of private legal costs in the case of Mr Valcke."

The investigation also found that Blatter, Valcke, former Argentina football federation president Julio Grondona and ex-Fifa finance director Markus Kattner had “set up a scheme through which they were allowing themselves to obtain extraordinary benefits with a minimum of effort".

‌



The statement added: "This vicious circle saw three of them (Blatter, Grondona and Valcke) signing the amendment contracts of the others and approving the respective extraordinary bonuses, while the fourth (Kattner) was in charge of implementing the payment of such bonuses (as well as of keeping the matter ‘off the books’, by not reflecting the bonuses in the Fifa financial statements and not reporting them to the Fifa auditors)."

Blatter had begun working at FIFA as technical director in 1975, becoming general secretary in 1981. He was elected as FIFA president in 1998 and retained his position in four subsequent elections before resigning in 2015.

The 2021 FIFA Ethics Committee ruling said: “Mr Blatter held the highest position in football as FIFA president and, as such, had a tremendous responsibility to serve the football community as a role model. By his conduct, the integrity and objectivity of FIFA have therefore been exceedingly violated. FIFA’s reputation has doubtlessly incurred serious and long-lasting damage.”

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola timeline emerges as Tottenham make their move for star
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola timeline emerges as Tottenham make their move for star

Liverpool could be set to speed up their transfer business with their tour of the USA now coming to an end

View 3 Images Liverpool's interest in Bradley Barcola remains strong (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool's need to dip into the transfer market has perhaps been exacerbated. The Reds wrapped up their pre-season tour of the USA on Sunday night with a chastening 4-2 defeat to Leeds United.

‌



The game was a Jekyll and Hyde-type performance from Andoni Iraola's side. Liverpool took a commanding 2-0 lead in the first half and looked in total control.

‌



Leeds then overpowered a much-changed Liverpool after the break and handed the Basque head coach his first defeat in charge. The aftermath has seen many fans across social media call for more recruits, with the Reds needing to address problems in defence and in attack before time runs out.

‌



Today's news sees the Bradley Barcola saga take a twist. Elsewhere, a Liverpool star has been targeted by Tottenham Hotspur.

Bradley Barcola timeline emerges

Fabrizio Romano has claimed that fresh contact will be made between the Reds and PSG this week. Speaking on his YouTube channel, he said, "new contacts [will be] prepared between Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain."

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



4 transfers Liverpool need to complete after Leeds defeat showed harsh reality READ MORE :

Liverpool handed Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG strike contingency plan READ MORE :

Reports have stated that Barcola is keen on a move to Anfield, despite also being admired by the likes of Arsenal. Romando added that "conversations will continue next week", but claimed no deal is imminent, giving the Reds a longer timeline to get the deal over the line.

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola has been linked with Liverpool (Image: Franco Arland, Getty Images)

PSG are said to be looking for around £145m for the French international, but Liverpool are believed to want to bring that price down significantly. Romano said there is a possibility this transfer could run all summer, adding that it now "depends on Liverpool, on how much they want to spend."

‌



Spurs in for Cody Gakpo

Spurs are reportedly interested in Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo, but the Reds are reluctant to part with the Dutch star. Sky Sports claims Liverpool would be willing to let Gakpo go if they could source a replacement.

The Netherlands international also has four years left on his deal, and talkSPORT has suggested that Liverpool are likely to demand around £70m for the player.

Gakpo made 52 appearances for Liverpool last term, scoring nine goals and bagging six assists. However, if he were to depart, without a replacement being sought, it would leave Liverpool with only teenager Rio Ngumoha and new signing Victor Munoz on the flanks.

‌



View 3 Images Cody Gakpo of Liverpool (Image: Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

Spurs have splashed out £237m this summer and manager Roberto De Zerbi has hinted more is to come. "The transfer market, it's not finished for sure, but we completed 60 per cent of our project in the transfer market. Now we have another bomba!" he told football.london last week.

Gakpo moved to Liverpool in January 2023 from PSV Eindhoven for around £37m. He has made 180 appearances for Liverpool, scoring 50 goals and providing 23 assists, winning the Premier League in 2025.
