World.title: Trump says Iran facing ‘last chance before decapitation’
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump said Monday that negotiations with Iran were ongoing despite Tehran’s denials and the Islamic Republic was facing a “last chance before decapitation.”

Trump, speaking to reporters at the White House, said he agreed to continue to pursue talks with Iran at the request of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and other countries.

Iran’s foreign ministry denied on Monday that negotiations with Washington were taking place, but Trump insisted they were. “We are talking right now,” he said.

“This is a last chance for them to sign a good document,” the US president added. “I want to give them every last chance before decapitation.”

The talks are focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which Trump said could come “literally by tomorrow,” and the denuclearization of Iran, which he said could “take a little while.”

Washington and Tehran have been at war since February 28, when the United States and Israel launched surprise strikes against Iran, though months of on-and-off diplomacy have led to periods of relative calm.

More than five months later, Iran remains able to fire missiles and drones at US and allied targets in the region and retains its enriched uranium stockpiles.

In what has become a familiar pattern, Trump last week had threatened to hit Iran “very hard” — potentially with renewed attacks against energy infrastructure — only to pull back on Saturday, saying the “perimeters” of a deal were there.

Iran, for its part, said it is not currently negotiating with the United States.

“Our negotiations are with Oman to secure passage through the Strait of Hormuz,” the critical oil corridor, foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said.

– Hormuz –

Hormuz has been a major sticking point in efforts to end the war. Since a ceasefire broke down, Iran has reprised a blockade of the waterway that it first imposed early in the war, obstructing vessels attempting to pass and firing on commercial ships.

Calling Tehran “duplicitous” for “openly and proudly” saying it was not negotiating, Trump wrote on social media: “Whether Iran wants to admit it or not, we are, in fact, talking of a solution to a problem that they have caused, for decades.”

He pointed to the United States’ counter-blockade of Iranian ports, adding: “Nothing gets through to Iran, unless we want it to, and nothing will get through, unless a Deal, or Total Surrender, is accomplished.”

Before the war, there was free passage through Hormuz, but Iran now insists on retaining control and charging fees, something the United States rejects.

Tehran has refused to let ships travel any route other than one that hugs the Iranian coast.

On Sunday, Baqaei told state television that a deal was close on managing Hormuz together with Oman, which sits on the other side of the narrow waterway.

“We are now going to reach an understanding on a route acceptable to both sides — neither the northern route nor the southern route — but one that respects the sovereign rights of both sides and safeguards our national interests and security,” he said.

But he insisted that such an agreement did not mean the reopening of the strait.

On Sunday, a tanker off the coast of Oman reported hearing an explosion nearby, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) Centre reported, but the ship and crew were all reported safe.

– Denuclearization ‘has to happen’ –

The US president said at the start of the conflict that the war was necessary to deal with Iran’s nuclear program and he repeated on Monday that “the denuclearization of Iran has to happen.”

Western nations accuse Iran of seeking a bomb, though Tehran insists the program is entirely civilian in nature.

Speaking to reporters on Air Force One over the weekend, Trump said he had been asked by Iran as well as regional US partners to hold off on further strikes, which he claimed would have been “the biggest attack since World War II.”

Iranian media denied that Tehran had asked Trump not to strike.

A previous ceasefire deal fell through last month. It was supposed to open the Strait of Hormuz to ships carrying vital energy exports from the Gulf to feed the global economy.

World.title: Iraq in talks with Iran to secure oil tanker passage through Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is holding discussions with Iran to ensure the smooth passage of oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair said on Monday, expressing optimism that the two sides could reach understandings in the coming days to protect Iraqi crude shipments.

Khudair’s remarks come a day after government spokesman Haider al-Aboudi said Iraqi officials had received assurances from Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian that Iraqi oil tankers would be exempt from restrictions in the strategic waterway. Al-Aboudi later acknowledged that the exemption had not materialized, saying Tehran continues to view the strait as one of its key sources of leverage in the current regional crisis.

In remarks carried by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), Khudair said Iraqi officials held political and economic discussions with Iran alongside Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s recent engagements.

He said the talks focused on facilitating the movement of Iraqi oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, adding that Baghdad hopes to reach broader understandings in the coming days that would ensure the safe and uninterrupted passage of shipments.

Khudair also announced that Iraq signed an important agreement with Turkey on Aug. 1, extending existing oil cooperation arrangements for one year while both sides prepare a long-term framework agreement.

According to the minister, the deal is intended to ensure continued exports of crude from the Kurdistan Region’s oil fields while also supporting a government plan to transport part of southern Iraq’s crude through the northern pipeline network.

He said the goal is to increase exports through the northern route to more than 700,000 barrels per day.

Khudair added that discussions held during the prime minister’s recent foreign engagements also focused on expanding broader economic cooperation and signing multiple memoranda of understanding with neighboring countries.

He said the government’s strategy is based on strengthening partnerships, investment, and regional cooperation to support Iraq’s economy.

The minister added that additional revenues generated from higher oil exports and improved contracts with international energy companies would be directed toward infrastructure projects in healthcare, education, transportation, and workforce development.

World.title: Zelensky sacks his ambassador to the US
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday dismissed his ambassador to the United States, Olga Stefanishyna, in a move that had been expected following a government reshuffle last month.

The sacking, announced by decree, happened however as Kyiv was lobbying Washington hard to obtain more Patriot air defence missiles to block Russian strikes.

In a Facebook post in which she also posted a letter asking to be relieved of her duties, Stefanishyna said the decision was her own and “dictated by personal circumstances”.

She called her posting to Washington “the greatest honour” of her life.

“We increased the supply of American weapons and maintained support precisely when the political climate in Washington was shifting against us,” she added.

Stefanishyna, a former deputy prime minister and justice minister, was nominated as ambassador in July last year.

The role is crucial for Ukraine, which depends on US arms deliveries and intelligence-sharing in the conflict against Russia.

Relations between Zelensky and his US counterpart Donald Trump have been strained and, at times, stormy.

But the billionaire Republican former real estate mogul has recently been more encouraging towards the Ukrainian leader.

According to Ukrainian media, Stefanishyna is under investigation by the country’s anti-corruption agency on suspicion of wrongdoing, although she has not been formally accused.

Zelensky, who made a controversial government reshuffle in July, has not yet announced who will replace Stefanishyna as ambassador in Washington.

World.title: Iraq oil exports hit by Hormuz closure and Kurdistan disruptions
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s state oil marketer SOMO has denied offering discounts on Iraqi crude, saying prices continue to be determined through competitive bidding despite disruptions caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and falling exports from the Kurdistan Region.

Speaking in an interview with journalist Mohammed Qais, SOMO Director Ali Nizar said Iraq sold 42 million barrels of crude in July, well below the approximately 105 million barrels per month exported before the current regional crisis.

Nizar dismissed reports that Iraq was selling crude at discounted prices to attract buyers. He said SOMO’s pricing policy relies on competition among companies capable of safely transporting cargoes through the Strait of Hormuz, where shipping has become more difficult due to higher insurance and transportation costs.

“Only a limited number of major international trading companies are currently able to transit the Strait safely,” Nizar said, adding that SOMO selects the highest bids submitted by qualified buyers and applies those prices to competing offers.

He argued that if Iraq were offering significant discounts, it would have been able to sell all of its available production.

According to Nizar, Iraq exported 35.5 million barrels through its southern terminals in July, while another 7 million barrels were shipped through Turkey’s Ceyhan port, bringing total monthly exports to 42 million barrels.

The figure marks an improvement from 24 million barrels exported in June but remains far below pre-crisis levels, when Iraq exported around 3.4 million barrels per day, equivalent to roughly 105 million barrels per month.

Nizar said Iraq and Turkey have reached a one-year agreement to continue using the Iraq-Turkey pipeline after the previous transit agreement expired on July 26.

Under the arrangement, Iraq will have guaranteed access to transport at least 750,000 barrels per day through the pipeline between Silopi and Ceyhan, which has a maximum capacity of 1.5 million barrels per day.

Turkey will be allowed to use any remaining capacity if Iraq does not fully utilize the pipeline, he added. Nizar also said British energy company BP, alongside a Turkish partner and future participation from U.S. companies, will help develop Kirkuk oil fields to boost production.

Nizar said attacks targeting oil fields in the Kurdistan Region have severely disrupted production, causing exports through Turkey to fall from 240,000 barrels per day to just 20,000 barrels per day.

He attributed the decline to foreign energy companies suspending operations because of security concerns.

To increase northern exports, the Oil Ministry is transporting crude from southern refineries to northern facilities by tanker trucks as part of a plan to eventually supply 1 million barrels per day to Turkey under the new bilateral agreement.

World.title: Iraq PM to visit Saudi Arabia next week
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi is expected to visit Saudi Arabia next week after international, regional, and domestic mediation efforts helped ease tensions between Baghdad and Riyadh, according to a report published Monday by a local news agency, citing an informed source.

The source said the diplomatic contacts over recent days succeeded in improving relations between the two countries, paving the way for the prime minister’s previously postponed visit.

According to the report, al-Zaidi’s visit will focus on security cooperation, economic relations, and investment opportunities.

The source also claimed Saudi Arabia intends to present the Iraqi prime minister with evidence it says shows that attacks targeting the Kingdom originated from Iraqi territory.

The reported visit comes days after al-Zaidi, who also serves as commander-in-chief of the armed forces, reiterated that Iraq will not allow its territory to be used to threaten neighboring countries. He also announced the formation of a joint security committee tasked with preventing future cross-border attacks and strengthening measures against potential violations.

Last Wednesday, the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) announced that American and Saudi warplanes had carried out precision strikes against weapons and logistics sites in eastern Iraq. CENTCOM said the targets belonged to Iran-linked armed groups responsible for attacks against Saudi Arabia.

Following those strikes, al-Zaidi postponed a planned visit to Riyadh that had been scheduled for the following day. The Iraqi government has not officially announced the date of the reported visit or confirmed the details cited by the source.

World.title: High temperatures cause ammunition depot to explode in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Summer scorching temperatures in Iraq caused an ammunition depot at Camp Taji north of Baghdad to explode on Sunday.

The Iraqi Ministry of Defense reported that a fire broke out inside a weapons and ammunition storage facility due to high summer temperatures.

The Iraqi Security Media Cell (ISMC) said in a statement that the high temperatures caused stored projectiles and explosives to explode, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Camp Taji is a large Iraqi military base located around 27 kilometers (17 miles) north of Baghdad. The camp formerly housed US-led international coalition soldiers until it was fully handed over to Iraqi authorities in 2020.

The specific storage contained heavy munitions belonging to the Iraqi army.

The explosion occurred during a severe regional heatwave. Temperatures in Baghdad hit 49 degrees Celsius (120 degrees Fahrenheit), while the neighboring areas reached 50 degrees Celsius.

Civil Defense units were dispatched quickly to contain the fire and keep it from spreading to other depots.

No immediate injuries or deaths have been reported.

Incidents of this type are common in Iraq because of the old infrastructure, poor safety regulations, and scorching summer temperatures.

World.title: 'Resignations are part of politics': DKS on two Congress MLAs quitting over Karnataka cabinet snub
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Tuesday downplayed the resignation of two Congress MLAs who quit the legislative assembly after being left out of the state cabinet expansion, saying "it is a part of politics.

"

Shivakumar said, "Resignations are a part of politics. No one can stop those who want to resign. If they want the party and a political future, they should stay."

Drawing from his own political journey, the chief minister said he too had been denied ministerial berths in the past but chose to remain with the party.

"If there is a party, everything else follows. When I was denied a ministerial berth during the tenures of Dharam Singh and Siddaramaiah, I could have resigned too.

Didn't G Parameshwara and I remain patient?" he said.

Shivakumar also said he had directed all ministers to immediately visit their respective districts to assess the drought relief situation.

The remarks came a day after Congress MLAs Yashavantarayagouda V Patil (Indi) and Belur Gopalakrishna (Sagar) resigned from the Karnataka Legislative Assembly, expressing disappointment over being excluded from the cabinet expansion.





Patil submitted his resignation to Deputy Speaker Rudrappa Lamani at the Vidhana Soudha. Soon after, his supporters staged a protest in Bengaluru, alleging that he had been treated unfairly by the party.

Gopalakrishna also resigned, adding to the pressure on the Congress leadership ahead of the swearing-in ceremony for the new ministers.

Speaking to reporters, Patil claimed his name had been included in the list of ministers until the last moment but was dropped from the final announcement.

"I have been watching the developments within the party; ultimately today, during the expansion, our leadership failed to keep the promise made. So, without any other option, it was inevitable for me to resign. I have submitted the resignation," he said.

World.title: Justice Manmohan Singh Liberhan, who probed Babri Masjid demolition, dies at 87
World.content:
Justice MS Liberhan (Picture from Haryana govt website)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Justice Manmohan Singh Liberhan, who headed the one-man commission that investigated the circumstances leading to the demolition of the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya, died on Sunday at the age of 87.Punjab and Haryana high court bar association President Rohit Sud confirmed his death, saying Justice Liberhan passed away in Chandigarh. His last rites will be held on Monday.Justice Liberhan began practising law at the Punjab and Haryana high court in 1964. He was elected to the Punjab and Haryana Bar Council in August 1970 and remained a member until February 11, 1987. During this period, he also served as the Bar Council's secretary from January 1976 to June 1983.He was elevated as a judge of the Punjab and Haryana high court on February 11, 1987. In July 1997, he was appointed Chief Justice of the Madras high court before taking over as Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh high court in February 1998.On December 16, 1992, days after the demolition of the Babri Masjid, the Centre appointed Justice Liberhan to head the one-man Liberhan Commission to probe the events leading up to the incident. The commission went on to become one of the longest-running inquiries in India's history.

World.title: CRPF officer kills two colleagues, injures one before killing self in Assam
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A CRPF officer allegedly shot dead two of his colleagues and injured another before killing himself at a camp in Assam's Nagaon district on Tuesday, police told news agency PTI.

The incident took place at the CRPF's 34 Battalion camp in Katimari, Nagaon, at around 7 am, when Assistant Sub-Inspector (GD) Ballani Premabaram, who was on duty at the main gate, allegedly opened fire on his colleagues, Nagaon Deputy Superintendent of Police (HQ) Paramita Sarkar told PTI.

Premabaram later turned the weapon on himself and died at the spot, she said.

Head Constable (GD) Vishnu Prasad Baghel and Sub-Inspector (GD) Ramnawal Singh Yadav were killed in the firing, while Assistant Sub-Inspector (Mane) Govind Sripul was injured and admitted to a private hospital for treatment.

World.content: Netaji Subhas Chandra Boseâs grandnephew Chandra Kumar Bose resigned from the TMC on Monday, citing personal reasons, months after joining the party ahead of the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections.

World.title: WhatsApp puts multiple accounts under review, temporarily blocks access for users
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Multiple WhatsApp users including several in India reported that their accounts had been placed "under review" for 24 hours, temporarily blocking access to the messaging platform's features without prior warning.

The disruption surfaced around 8pm IST on Monday, with affected users sharing screenshots showing a message from the Meta-owned app stating that their accounts were being reviewed to verify compliance with WhatsApp's terms of service. The notification read that account activity and device information were being checked and that users would typically receive a decision within 24 hours.

Responding a report by PTI, a WhatsApp spokesperson acknowledged that errors can occur while enforcing the platform's safety measures.

"We are always working to stay ahead of those trying to abuse our service and ban accounts to help keep other users safe. Sometimes we get this wrong and if we do, we try to fix it as quickly as possible to get people back to chatting," the spokesperson said.

The app also directed affected users to guidance on responsible use of WhatsApp and information relating to stolen phones and accounts.

Several users took to social media to complain that their accounts had been disabled despite using the official version of the app.





One user wrote: "My WhatsApp account has been disabled without any explanation. I have already submitted an appeal, but the review page only displays a generic message stating that it will 'typically be reviewed within 24 hours'. Help me urgently."

Another user, identified as Saloni on X, posted: "My WhatsApp account was suddenly disabled without any warning. I only use the official app, and my work depends on WhatsApp.

Please help. This was so unnecessary."

The temporary account reviews come as WhatsApp remains under government scrutiny in India over its proposed username feature, which would allow users to communicate without sharing their phone numbers.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The Centre recently received WhatsApp's response to a notice seeking clarification on the feature, which officials fear could increase phishing, impersonation, online fraud and so-called digital arrest scams.

The government has directed the company not to roll out the feature in India until consultations are completed.

WhatsApp has maintained that the feature is still under development and will be introduced gradually later this year. The company has said users will still need a phone number to create an account and that several safeguards, including protections against impersonation and limits on unsolicited contact, have been built into the feature.

World.title: Govt proposes mandatory Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication systems from Oct 2028 to cut road crashes
World.content:
All new cars, passenger and goods vehicles would need to have Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication system. (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From Oct 2028, all new two- and three-wheelers, cars, passenger and goods vehicles (including buses and trucks) would need to have Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication system, as per a draft notification of the road transport ministry. The V2V technology is being rolled out to curb collisions and accidents.The recently published draft notification by road transport ministry proposes phased implementation of the V2V communication system and to start with all vehicles in categories L (two- and three-wheelers), M (passenger vehicles) and N (goods vehicles) manufactured from Oct 2027 would be required to comply with the newly-notified automotive standard, AIS-230, wherever they are equipped with V2V communication systems.The technology enables real-time exchange of speed, direction, position, and braking data between vehicles to prevent collisions at blind curves, intersections, or from drivers coming the wrong way without needing a cellular network. Each vehicle needs to be fitted with a device that will automatically detect approaching vehicles for preventing any crash.Unlike conventional vehicle-safety systems, which primarily depend on onboard sensors and driver reaction, V2V communication can provide information beyond the direct line of sight.âIt is therefore expected to complement Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and support proactive accident prevention, connected mobility and future intelligent transport applications,â the ministry said.In this case, every vehicle fitted with the V2V communication system will continuously send out their locations, speed and direction as tiny radio signals. They will also relay information on sudden braking by a vehicle ahead, forward collision risks, unsafe lane changes, wrong-way driving and the approach of emergency vehicles.The receiving vehicleâs system compares this information with its own location, speed and direction to predict a possible collision and alerts the driver for action.At a later stage, govt will also roll out the Vehicle to Infrastructure (V2I) communication system. In this case, sensors are installed with infrastructure, such as signal and power poles, edges of bridges and flyovers, and barricaded areas to alert vehicles.

World.title: 21 Bangladesh nationals detained in J&K’s Ramban
World.content:
JAMMU: At least 21 Bangladesh nationals, including four women and seven minors, were detained in J&Kâs Ramban district last week. Officials were questioning them to learn who facilitated their movement to the Union Territory, official sources said Monday.

The group was caught moving in two vehicles during a checking drive in Banihal on Aug 1, as no vehicle apart from those in Amarnath convoys is currently being allowed to move towards Kashmir in view of rain-triggered landslides and mudslides.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Those detained are aged between two years and 38 years. âUpon verification, none of them could produce any valid identity or travel document establishing their lawful entry into or presence within Indian territory,â said an official source.

âDuring preliminary questioning, the detained individuals disclosed that they had crossed the international border and entered India through Assam, from where they travelled to Jammu via train. They were moving towards Kashmir in search of employment,â the source added.

Investigators were probing whether any local or interstate network was involved in assisting the movement of these illegal immigrants.

World.title: J&K: Days after Kulgam terror attack, man with grenade held in Pulwama
World.content:
Kulgam: Security personnel keep a vigil during an inspection of vehicles to maintain public safety following the recent terror attack in Anantnag, at Qaimoh, Kulgam district, Jammu and Kashmir.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: A suspect was arrested Monday in J&Kâs Pulwama with a hand grenade, three âanti-nationalâ posters and a mobile phone during a security overdrive spurred by last weekâs killings of two migrant labourers in a terror attack in neighbouring Kulgam.Police identified the man as Tousef Ahmad Dar, a local, and booked him under several laws, including the stringent Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).Authorities claimed Dar was spotted walking towards a checkpoint set up jointly by J&K police, Army and CRPF and began to flee after noticing the security forces. Dar was chased down by troopers and caught some distance away, the police said.âThe police remain committed to maintaining peace and security and will continue to take firm action against individuals involved in anti-national and unlawful activities,â the police said in a statement.The checkpoint where Dar was spotted is one of many across Kashmir that have come up after the killings of the two migrant workers on July 31.Earlier, on July 23, a terrorist shot dead a J&K head constable, Ashiq Hussain Qureshi, in south Kashmirâs Anantnag. It was the first attack in Kashmir since the Pahalgam massacre that left 26 people, most of them tourists, dead on April 22 last year. The police said Lashkar-e-Toiba offshoot The Resistance Front (TRF) was involved in both the Kulgam and Anantnag attacks.On Monday, Kashmir IG VK Birdi reviewed security and ordered robust counter-insurgency measures. âHe (Virdi) stressed seamless coordination among all agencies. The IGP also reviewed security for highways, rail tracks and stations across the Valley. He directed officers to place âdynamic nakasâ and ensure enhanced foot patrolling, particularly at night, at vulnerable locations and inter-district boundaries,â a police spokesman said.

World.title: Opposition MPs protest in Parliament complex on Ram temple donation theft issue, police action against students
World.content:
Opposition MPs, including Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, protested in Parliament House complex on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) against the theft of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya and "police excesses" against student protesters.

Carrying placards against the government, MPs protested in front of the Makar Dwar of Parliament with slogans such as 'chhanda chor, gaddi chor' and 'Amit Shah jawaab do' raised.

The MPs also kept donation boxes at the spot to symbolise the alleged theft of donations at the Ram temple and lined up around them to raise slogans against the government. Some MPs also put cash in the box to symbolise the donations made and "theft" that took place later.

Besides Priyanka Gandhi, SP's Dimple Yadav and Dharmendra Yadav, TMC's Sagarika Ghose, RJD's Sanjay Yadav and Manoj Jha, RSP's NK Premchandran, among others, participated in the protest.

The protesting MPs lined up behind a big banner that read 'Why Amit Shah absent from Parliament', and raised slogans against the Home Minister.

The INDIA bloc has vowed to corner the government on issues of alleged theft of donations at the Ram temple and the use of "brutal force" against students during their protests last week.

Earlier in the day, INDIA bloc parties' floor leaders met in Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge's chamber in the Parliament complex, and vowed to corner the government on the two issues of "chhanda chori" and "police excesses" against students.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 12 LIVE: Opposition MPs raise slogans on Ram Temple donation theft issue in RS; LS adjourned till 2 p.m.
World.content:
Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman is set to introduce the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha on Tuesday (August 4, 2026), according to the revised List of Business issued by the House.

The Bill seeks to further amend the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, the Income-tax Act, 2025, and the Finance Act, 2026. Sitharaman will move for leave to introduce the legislation and subsequently introduce the Bill in the House.

A day earlier, on Monday (August 3, 2026), the Lok Sabha passed a Bill to increase the sanctioned strength of judges in the Supreme Court without any discussion as persistent protests by Opposition members over the police action against protesting students at Jantar Mantar and the alleged chadhawa chori (theft of offerings) at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya continued to disrupt proceedings. Meanwhile, the Rajya Sabha passed the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026.

World.title: Telangana’s Sircilla weaver crafts matchbox-size handloom saree in 170 minutes
World.content:
Ahead of National Handloom Day slated for August 7, Sircilla district-based handloom weaver Veldi Hariprasad showcased his skill and precision by weaving a saree — that could fit into a matchbox — in just 170 minutes, in Telangana’s textile town on Monday (August 3, 2026).

The unique feat was performed on a traditional handloom in the presence of local residents and several members of the weaving community. It drew appreciation for Mr. Hariprasad’s skill and perseverance while highlighting Sircilla’s rich handloom heritage.

Mr. Hariprasad said he had woven the 5.5-metre-long and 45-inch-wide saree weighing 175 grams using traditional weaving techniques.

Those who witnessed the feat described it as incredible and expressed hope that such efforts would help promote the region’s age-old handloom traditions and preserve them for future generations.

Mr. Hariprasad has earlier earned wide appreciation for weaving special sarees based on themes such as ‘Nari Shakti’ and ‘Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav’.

World.title: Virtual queue system for darshan begins at Guruvayur temple in Kerala
World.content:
Sreekrishna Temple, Guruvayur, Kerala, on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) rolled out its much-awaited virtual queue system for darshan, marking a major step towards ensuring a smoother and more organised pilgrimage experience.

The system was inaugurated by Guruvayur Devaswom chairman A.V. Gopinath at a function held near the entrance to the Bhagavathy shrine at the temple’s East Nada around 6.30 a.m.

Despite intermittent rain and inclement weather, more than 100 devotees successfully had darshan through the virtual queue during the first slot from 7 a.m. to 8 a.m. As many as 1,800 devotees had booked virtual queue slots up to 1 p.m.

Under the trial arrangement, devotees must report at the designated virtual queue entrance — located at the northern end of the queue complex at the East Nada — at least 30 minutes before their scheduled time. They must carry the booking receipt and the same government-issued identification document used while making the online reservation, as it will be verified by security personnel.

For the trial phase, virtual queue darshan will be available on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 7 a.m. to noon, and again from 4 p.m. to 5 p.m. Around 300 devotees will be allowed entry during each one-hour slot.

World.title: DMK youth wing says Udhayanidhi arrested to prevent him from raising questions in Assembly
World.content:
The DMK youth wing on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) condemned the arrest of its leader, Udhayanidhi Stalin, alleging the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government had resorted to the action instead of responding to the questions he had raised over its handling of the Cauvery water dispute.

In a statement, the youth wing said the arrest reflected the government’s “helplessness”.

“Mr. Udhayanidhi did not refer to any individual in his speech. It is others who are twisting his remarks by claiming they were vulgar and contained double entendres. As it is not in a position to answer the questions to be raised by the Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly session, the government has chosen to arrest him instead,” the statement contended.

The youth wing further alleged that if the dialogues delivered by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay in his films were compiled, they would contain language more objectionable than Mr. Udhayanidhi’s speech.

“Even in his last film, he uttered swear words,” the statement claimed. It also accused the TVK of failing to condemn BJP leader Nainar Nagenthran for allegedly making remarks linking an actor with the Chief Minister.

The DMK youth wing maintained that the arrest was politically motivated and intended to divert attention from the State government’s response to the Cauvery issue.

World.title: Overnight downpour lashes Telangana between August 3 and August 4 morning; Kamareddy records 182.8 mm rainfall
World.content:
Heavy overnight rain lashed several parts of Telangana, including Hyderabad, between Monday (August 3, 2026) and Tuesday (August 4, 2026) morning, with some locations recording more than 100 mm of rainfall.

In Hyderabad, the overnight downpour led to waterlogging in several parts of the city, particularly in the eastern and southern stretches. As rainwater flooded roads, Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency and DRF teams were on the ground to clear the waterlogging points including at Rajendranagar, Masab Tank, Quthbullapur, and Attapur.

Rain intensity in & around Hyderabad

According to data from the Telangana Development Planning Society (TGDPS) as of 8 a.m. on Tuesday (August 4, 2026), Saroornagar recorded the highest rainfall in the city at 113 mm, followed by Alkapuri at 109.5, LB Nagar at 95.8, mm, 83.8 mm in Chandrayangutta, 83.5 mm in Bandlaguda, 80.5 mm in Nagole, 80.3 mm in Vanasthalipuram, 71.8 mm in Hayathnagar, 70.5 mm in Adibatla, and 70 mm in Shamshabad.

Power outage

Electricity went on a blink for hours together in some areas forcing residents to take to social media to raise the issue. “Power cut since YESTERDAY in Jai Hind Nagar Colony, Shaikpet, Hyderabad — many hours with no power and no update. We pay our electricity bills and taxes on time, yet left completely in the dark. This is unacceptable for a city like Hyderabad. Restore power NOW,” wrote one resident on X.

"@tgspdcl Power cut since YESTERDAY in Jai Hind Nagar Colony, Shaikpet, Hyderabad — many hours with no power and no update. We pay our electricity bills and taxes on time, yet left completely in the dark. This is unacceptable for a city like Hyderabad. Restore power NOW. — Imran Khan (@yourskhanimran) August 3, 2026

The rains were considerably heavier in parts of the State, with Kamareddy district receiving some of the highest rainfall during the period. TGDPS data showed that Kamareddy recorded 182.8 mm of rainfall as of 8 a.m., the highest among the locations reported. This was followed by 127 mm in Pitlam (Kamareddy), 124.8 mm in Maqdumpur (Kamareddy), 118 mm in Sarvapur (Kamareddy), 115 mm in Kodangal (Vikarabad), 110 mm in Sirgapoor (Sangareddy) and 105.8 mm in Tekulapally (Bhadradri Kothagudem).

World.title: Congress stalling Parliament, blocking debate on key Bills: BJP
World.content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) accused the Congress and its INDIA bloc allies of deliberately disrupting the Monsoon Session of Parliament, alleging that their conduct has prevented discussions on key Bills and exposed the Opposition's "double standards" on issues such as paper leaks and student protests.

Parliament Monsoon Session Day 12 updates

Addressing a press conference at the party headquarters in New Delhi, BJP national spokesperson and Lok Sabha MP Sambit Patra alleged that despite crores of rupees being spent on every session of Parliament, Question Hour and Zero Hour have been repeatedly disrupted, depriving MPs of an opportunity to raise issues concerning their constituencies.

"The way the 2026 Monsoon Session of Parliament is progressing, and the manner in which the Congress party, along with some of its alliance partners, is disrupting the session, is a matter of serious concern. Crores of rupees are spent on every session of Parliament.”

"However, ever since the session began, Question Hour has not taken place in Parliament. Disruptions are being created during Zero Hour as well," Mr. Patra told reporters.

"Hardly any Bill is being discussed. The reason behind this is the conduct of the Congress party and some of its INDIA alliance partners. I am genuinely surprised by their double standards," he said, adding that the Opposition might not allow Parliament to function on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) as well.

Targeting the Congress over its alleged "double standards" on paper leak cases, Mr. Patra claimed the party remains silent on such incidents in States where it is in power while politicising similar issues elsewhere.

Referring to Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge's reported remarks on the alleged police constable recruitment examination irregularities, Mr. Patra alleged, "Priyank Kharge said students should first go on a 25-day hunger strike, after which they would be lathi-charged and only then would he think about resigning. Rahul Gandhi continues to remain silent on this."

Mr. Patra also alleged that the Congress has ignored students protesting over the alleged paper leak in the 14th JPSC examination in Jharkhand.

"No Congress MP was seen holding a placard on the JPSC examination issue at Makar Dwar. This is selective outrage driven only by political interests," he claimed.

The BJP leader further alleged that repeated disruptions have prevented meaningful discussions on important Bills passed by Parliament, depriving the public of information about legislative reforms.

He said Bills such as the Supreme Court Number of Judges (Amendment) Bill, 2026 and the Registration of Birth and Death (Amendment) Bill, 2026 were passed without adequate discussion because of the Opposition's protests.

Mr. Patra also slammed the Opposition over its recent protest inside the Parliament complex on the alleged theft of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya, alleging that it insulted Hindu saints and hurt religious sentiments.

He alleged that portraying a person dressed as a sadhu as a thief and dragging him during the protest sent a wrong message about the Hindu religious community.

"Coming dressed as a sadhu, portraying sadhus as thieves and dragging them inside the premises of the country's highest democratic institution sends a message to villages that all sadhus are thieves. Had any other religion's religious leaders been portrayed in this manner, there would have been outrage across the world," Mr. Patra alleged.

World.title: Public drinking and unruly groups: Kadapa police deploy drones at Gandikota
World.content:
The Kadapa district police have stepped up surveillance at the famed Gandikota tourist spot in the Jammalamadugu constituency, with the twin objectives of tackling crime and ensuring the safety of visitors.

Gandikota is often called the Indian equivalent of the Grand Canyon, where the Penna cleaves through a huge wall-like hill. The spot also houses an ancient fort and a 16th century temple, which are thronged by history, art and archaeology enthusiasts. The gorge is a favourite haunt of adventure lovers, especially the young.

Youth on motorcycles arrive here for the weekend even from the neighbouring States of Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu.

The police have started flying drone cameras to identify and catch anti-social elements moving in the vicinity of the gorge. The police have taken serious note of the frequent movement of unruly groups that drink in public and cause inconvenience to tourists, especially families.

“As it is quite difficult for the cops to physically roam around the vast stretches of rocky terrain, we have taken to drone surveillance to ensure quick identification of culprits with surgical precision,” Kadapa Superintendent of Police Nachiket Vishwanath Shelke told The Hindu.

Drone camera keeps watch over Gandikota



The Jammalamadugu police have put a drone over Gandikota in Kadapa district to track anti-social elements at the tourist site.



Video: Special Arrangement pic.twitter.com/yaqC1ejodZ — The Hindu - Andhra Pradesh (@THAndhra) August 4, 2026

The trend of college students from the nearby Proddatur, Mydukur, Jammalamadugu and Allagadda towns skipping classes and visiting this tourist spot has also picked up, causing considerable worry to the law enforcers.

Last year, a college student was found dead at Gandikota, and the case remains unsolved.

Though there are a number of CCTV cameras along the road leading to Gandikota, which provide data on the inward and outward movement of vehicles, the department remained clueless on the movement of visitors inside the zone, which is mostly unmanned.

It was perhaps to fill this gap that drone surveillance has been taken up in this remote location abutting the gorge.

World.title: Pakistan to host Iranian officials as Trump’s patience wears thin
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakis­tan on Monday invited Iran’s parliament speaker and foreign minister for urgent consultations on regional developments, as Tehran described Islamabad as its primary mediator with the US.

National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq invited Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran’s chief negotiator with Washington and speaker of parliament. Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, meanwhile, invited his Iranian counterpart, Seyyed Abbas Araghchi. The invitations were delivered in Tehran late Monday night after Dar spoke with Araghchi.

“They exchanged views on regional and international developments, including the deteriorating situation in Occupied East Jerusalem,” the Foreign Office said in a statement.

It remained unclear when Ghalibaf and Araghchi would travel to Pakistan. A diplomatic source said both men had been asked to come as soon as possible for discussions on regional and international developments. Araghchi was in Iraq on Monday for Arbaeen, which is being observed on Tuesday.

The invitations came roughly 36 hours after US President Donald Trump announced he had canceled imminent strikes against Iran. Trump said allies had urged him to hold off because a deal appeared imminent.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke with Trump and persuaded him to call off the planned military action. Trump had also named UAE and Qatar as among the countries that had asked him to cancel the planned strikes.

Iran has been holding talks with Oman about the future of the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian authorities say they are close to an agreement but have not indicated whether the waterway would reopen or remain closed.

Pakistan has been relatively quiet on the mediation front compared with earlier efforts that produced the Islamabad MoU. It has, however, remained engaged through back channels with Iran and, together with Qatar, proposed a ceasefire plan during a nearly 13-day period of escalation.

Iran’s foreign ministry on Monday insisted that Pakistan is the main mediator with US. Spokesman Esmail Baqaei said: “The mediator in the discussions related to Iran and the US is Pakistan, and Qatar also helps in cases where necessary. To say that we have added a new mediator to the existing mediators is not, in the strict sense of the word, the case.”

Meanwhile, President Donald Trump accused Iran’s leadership of being “unbelievably duplicitous” after Tehran denied that any negotiations were underway with the US. The exchange renewed threats from Trump, who warned Iran faced “decapitation” and said he would keep up military pressure until there was a “deal, or total surrender”.

“I think we’re going to maybe get something, but I want to give them every last chance before decapitation,” Trump said, reiterating his threat to launch a major attack on Iran.

The war of words follows a familiar pattern in the five-month conflict between Washington and Tehran.

The president, who on Sunday said renewed talks would begin “tomorrow afternoon” without naming a venue or participants, added that the US Navy maintains complete control over the Strait of Hormuz.

“Nothing gets through to Iran, unless we want it to, and nothing will get through, unless a deal, or total surrender, is accomplished,” he said.

Trump had told reporters aboard Air Force One that Iran, along with Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar, had asked him to hold off on what he claimed would have been “the biggest attack since World War II”.

“Would I rather make a deal? I’m not looking to kill people,” Trump said on Sunday. He described ongoing discussions as a “last chance for them to sign a good document”.

With input from Agencies

Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

World.title: Govt slashes petrol price by Rs4.08, high-speed diesel by Rs2.45
World.content:
The government on Monday slashed the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4.08 and Rs2.45 per litre, respectively, passing on the impact of falling oil prices after US President Donald Trump called off a planned attack on Iran and announced talks with it.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs331.95 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs389.93 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs110 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs96 per litre on diesel.

The Petroleum Division’s notification said the new prices would be applicable for August 4 (Tuesday).

The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Pakistan gets a pass on new US visa bond rule
World.content:
• Washington makes visa bond programme permanent; Bangladesh, Nepal among 50 countries covered, India also excluded

• Visitors from listed nations face refundable deposits of up to $20,000

WASHINGTON: Pakistan is not among the 50 countries whose citizens may now be required to deposit up to $20,000 as a financial guarantee before obtaining a US visitor visa under a new programme that took effect on Aug 1.

The list published in the US Federal Register does not include Pakistan. Among South Asian countries, Bangladesh and Nepal are covered by the programme, while India is not.

Afghanistan and Iran are not included because the United States does not maintain normal diplomatic relations with either country.

The State Department said the decision followed a review of the 2025 pilot programme, which it said significantly reduced visa overstays among travellers from participating countries and improved compliance with US immigration rules. Officials said those findings prompted Washington to make the programme permanent.

According to the department, there were 45,488 overstays from these 50 countries in 2024. In the first 10 months of the pilot, the number of overstays was fewer than 50. The visa bond requirement has also resulted in a decrease in visa issuance, as some applicants appear to self-select by not paying a bond.

Diplomatic sources also confirmed to Dawn that “Pakistan is not on the list of countries covered by the programme”.

The programme applies to applicants for B-1 business and B-2 tourist visas from countries covered by the scheme. Under the new rules, US consular officers may require selected applicants to post a refundable bond of between $10,000 and $20,000 before issuing a visa.

The regulations make permanent a visa bond pilot launched in 2025 after the US State Department concluded that it had helped reduce visa overstays.

The new rules also increase the maximum bond from $15,000 to $20,000 and eliminate the previous $5,000 minimum bond available during the pilot programme.

The 50 countries covered by the programme include 30 African nations as well as countries in Asia, the Caribbean and the Pacific.

The bond will be refunded if the visitor complies with all visa conditions and leaves the United States before the authorised period of stay expires. Applicants who overstay or otherwise violate the terms of their visas risk forfeiting the deposit.

The bond requirement does not apply automatically to all applicants from the countries covered by the programme. Instead, US consular officers will determine on a case-by-case basis whether a bond is warranted before issuing a visa.

Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

World.title: PCB appoints South Africa's Michael Smith as batting coach for Pakistan men's cricket team
World.content:
Former South African cricketer Michael Smith has been appointed as the batting coach of the Pakistan men’s cricket team for two years, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) announced on Tuesday.

According to a press release issued by the PCB, the “46-year-old will work with the team across both red-ball and white-ball formats”.

He will join the Pakistan team ahead of the three-match Test series against England, commencing on Aug 19, the press release stated.

Elaborating on Smith’s experience, the press release stated that he had featured in 89 first-class matches, 72 List-A matches and 16 T20 matches between 2003 and 2013.

“The right-handed batter scored 7,029 runs across the three formats, including nine centuries and 40 half-centuries,” the PCB said.

Smith, who holds a Level 4 coaching qualification, has served on the coaching staffs of three HBL Pakistan Super League (PSL) franchises — Islamabad United, Karachi Kings and Multan Sultans, it added

The press release further stated that he has also worked as a batting coach with Australian franchise Hobart Hurricanes and Cricket Tasmani.

As a coaching consultant, Smith has worked with South Africa’s KZN Inland and Eastern Province, the press release added.

Prior to Smith’s appointment, former Test batter Asad Shafiq was appointed as Pakistan’s interim batting coach in April 2026 for the Bangladesh Test series. Shafiq is currently also accompanying the Pakistan team for its two-match Test series in the West Indies.

Additional input from Mohammad Yaqoob

World.title: Trump's Board of Peace reassures Israel after Tel Aviv's objections on Gaza pullout
World.content:
US President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace on Monday assured Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Israel’s withdrawal from Gaza would only begin after Hamas’s complete disarmament, following his objections.

Two members of Netanyahu’s security cabinet had urged a vote to tear up the deal championed by Trump after the board released a text that called for Israel to begin a phased withdrawal.

Netanyahu’s office said it had raised concerns to the United States, after Trump on Friday hailed as a “major milestone” an agreement by Hamas to hand over weapons to a nascent Palestinian governing committee.

Nickolay Mladenov, the high representative for Gaza under the Board of Peace, met with Netanyahu on Monday for what he acknowledged was difficult work.

But the board said it had reached a “common understanding of the shared objectives” with Israel.

Israel’s withdrawal beyond the Yellow Line, which demarcates the area in which Hamas still has control, “will take place only once decommissioning [of weapons] is complete, as Hamas committed to the mediators”, the board said on X.

Even if Israel withdraws under the plan, it would maintain control of much of Gaza under a Trump-led October ceasefire.

Hamas said late on Monday that it was adhering to “what was agreed upon regarding the implementation of the second phase of the ceasefire agreement, including the commitments of all parties”.

The group was “awaiting a clear and official response” from Mladenov and the mediators on what was agreed upon, according to the statement posted on Telegram.

Trump-Netanyahu gap

Israel had objected to the board’s Thursday text that called for a phased withdrawal within the territory and the immediate cessation of Israeli strikes in Gaza.

“Israel has conveyed its comments and concerns on the proposed framework to our American counterparts. The version that has been made public does not reflect Israel’s positions,” Doron Spielman, spokesman for the prime minister’s office, told AFP ahead of the Mladenov meeting.

Far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich had said that the text was “completely different” to the one presented to Netanyahu’s security cabinet and, along with a colleague, had demanded that the cabinet “immediately” hold a new vote on the Gaza plan.

Trump had earlier said that Israel was “very happy” about the disarmament announcement by Hamas.

It was the latest sign of disconnect between Trump and Netanyahu, who faces a tough re-election fight in October and has heavily promoted his relationship with the US leader, whom he met again in Washington last week.

Backtracking on announcement

Trump and Netanyahu have also been at loggerheads on Iran, with Israel sceptical of his attempts at diplomacy to end the war the two countries launched in late February.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog, who holds a largely ceremonial role, offered a more upbeat take on Trump’s Gaza efforts, saying the latest development marked “a very positive step with the clear caveat and undertaking that Hamas must be disarmed”.

Mohammad Dahlan, a senior Palestinian political figure who has played a key role in the Gaza plan, said after the Board of Peace roadmap that he had spoken to Trump’s son-in-law and aide Jared Kushner, who told him that Israel would end strikes in Gaza effective on Sunday.

But he quickly revised his social media post, instead saying that Kushner was “working with the Israeli side to halt the attacks” in Gaza.

He later accused Netanyahu of working “to obstruct the most promising opportunity to begin ending this war”.

On Monday evening, an Israeli strike on a vehicle west of Gaza City killed two Palestinians and injured several others, according to Mahmoud Bassal, a spokesperson for the civil defence rescue service. The Israeli military told AFP it targeted two fighters in the strike.

On Sunday, Israeli attacks killed 19 Palestinians, including women and children, according to the civil defence.

Qatar, Egypt and Turkey, which are mediating the truce in Gaza, late on Monday criticised Israel after renewed strikes in the Palestinian territory.

They strongly condemned what they said were “ongoing Israeli violations in the Gaza Strip, particularly the targeting of health facilities and infrastructure, and the casualties among civilians, including women and children”.

World.title: Heavy rain warning raises flood risk in low-lying areas
World.content:
• Medium to high flows expected in nullahs linked to Jhelum, Chenab and Ravi

• Authorities on high alert as NDMA reviews flood preparedness

LAHORE: While rising river flows have pushed Tarbela Dam near its maximum capacity, the Met Office has warned of urban flooding and inundation in low-lying areas of several cities as heavy monsoon rains are expected on Tuesday (today).

According to the Flood Forecasting Divi­sion (FFD) of the Pakistan Meteorological De­­­­partment, heavy rainfall may trigger wat­er accumulation in low-lying areas of Islam­abad, Rawalpindi, Lahore, Sheikhupura, Kasur, Faisalabad, Multan, Sahiwal, Okara, Bahawalnagar, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Sialkot, the Potohar region, Peshawar and Nowshera.

The division also warned of flash flooding in hill torrents and local streams across Kashmir, Murree, Galiyat, northeastern Punjab, Islamabad, the Potohar region, some areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Dera Ghazi Khan. Medium to high flows are expected in nullahs linked to the Jhelum, Chenab and Ravi rivers, while flash floods are also likely in the hill torrents of Dera Ghazi Khan, streams in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the Kabul River and its tributaries, and parts of northern Balochistan.

Landslides are also feared in the mountainous districts of upper Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, including Dir, Swat, Kohistan, Buner, Battagram, Mansehra, Shangla and Abbottabad, as well as Murree, Galiyat and the hilly areas of Azad Kashmir.

The FFD said the Indus River at Kalabagh, Guddu and Sukkur, and the Ravi at Balloki, are currently flowing at low flood level. It urged all relevant authorities to remain on alert and take precautionary measures to deal with possible rain-related emergencies.

According to the Water and Power Development Authority’s (Wapda) daily water report, the Indus at Tarbela recorded inflows of 250,700 cusecs and outflows of 191,900 cusecs on Monday. The Kabul River at Nowshera recorded both inflows and outflows of 43,700 cusecs, while the Jhelum at Mangla registered inflows of 44,700 cusecs and outflows of 7,000 cusecs. The Chenab at Marala recorded inflows of 85,900 cusecs and outflows of 69,900 cusecs.

The report showed that Tarbela Dam’s water level had risen to 1,543 feet, only seven feet below its maximum conservation level of 1,550 feet, with live storage reaching 5.178 million acre-feet (MAF). Mangla Dam’s water level stood at 1,199.35 feet, around 42 feet below its maximum conservation level of 1,242 feet, with live storage of 4.193 MAF.

Chashma Reservoir is also nearing full capacity, with its water level recorded at 648.50 feet against a maximum conservation level of 649 feet.

Monsoon, flood preparedness

Meanwhile, National Disaster Manage­me­­nt Authority (NDMA) Chairman retired Lt Gen Inam Haider Malik visited the Punjab Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) headquarters to review monsoon and flood preparedness across the province.

He was received by Punjab Minister Kha­waja Salman Rafique and PDMA Director General Saif Anwar Jappa. The NDMA chairman visited the Provincial Emergency Control Centre, where officials briefed him on preparedness measures, while climate change, resource management and capacity building also came under discussion.

Mr Rafique said all departments, including health, rescue and livestock, were fully mobilised to respond to any flood emergency. He said Rescue 1122 had been equipped with modern equipment worth billions of rupees, while new warehouses were being established across Punjab to improve emergency response.

The NDMA chairman said the authority was maintaining close coordination with all provinces and that PDMA, Rescue 1122 and other institutions were responding effectively to the evolving monsoon situation.

The PDMA director general said officials were continuously monitoring river flows and the monsoon situation across the province. He said underground water storage tanks were being constructed to reduce urban flooding, while Wasa had been equipped with modern machinery and its operations expanded to 41 cities. During the visit, the NDMA chairman presented commemorative shields to Mr Rafique and Mr Jappa.

World.title: Govt executes agreements with pension fund managers
World.content:
• 16 companies to establish separate pension funds, ensure death and disability risk cover for employees

• Centre to establish non-banking finance company to assist in implementation, monitoring of pension scheme

ISLAMABAD: The government has executed agreements with 16 pension fund managers to formally operationalise the Defined Contribution Pension Fund Scheme (DCPFS) launched a year ago for public sector employees as part of major pension reforms aimed at containing the snowballing pension burden on the budget.

In an announcement, the Ministry of Finance said it had executed agreements with 16 eligible pension fund managers, most of them banks and insurance companies. Around 10 of these eligible fund managers are owned or led by major commercial banks in the country.

They include ABL Asset Management Company, Al Habib Asset Management, Al Meezan Investment, Faysal Asset Management, JS Investments, MCB Investment, Alfalah Asset Management, HBL Asset Management, UBL Fund Managers and NBP Fund Management,

The pension fund managers led by or owned by insurance companies include EFU Life Assurance and Pak-Qatar Family Takaful. The remaining funds — Atlas Asset Man­agement, Lucky Invest­ments, National Investments and AWT Investments are owned by various business groups.

Under the agreements and rules, these fund managers would set up, operate and manage conventional or Shariah-compliant funds for state employees under the federal government-defined contributory pension fund scheme in accordance with the Voluntary Pension System Rules 2005.

Only these eligible pension fund managers shall be authorised to launch and manage employer pension funds for which the government will ensure annual budgetary allocation for the employer’s contribution. The agreements entail standard terms and conditions for providing systems support and electronic transfer of contributions to the pension fund’s designated bank accounts and further allocation of units to the relevant sub-funds in each employee’s pension account as per the allocation policy.

The agreements also envisage a mandatory insurance plan, providing death and disability risk cover to the employees, to be arranged by these fund managers.

The eligible pension fund managers will establish separate pension funds, while the government is responsible for the creation of a Non-Banking Finance Company (NBFC) to assist in implementation and monitoring of the pension fund scheme. Till such time the NBFC is established and fully operationalised, the government itself, through the finance ministry, will perform the NBFC role and establish an online portal to facilitate opening of pension accounts of employees, obtain information and data from eligible pension fund managers or otherwise communicate with the fund managers.

Under the rules, employees will not withdraw any amount from the pension account before retirement is notified. Even upon reaching retirement age, the employee shall not withdraw more than 25pc of the accumulated balance in the pension account, and shall invest the remaining amount in the manner prescribed in the Voluntary Pension System Rules, 2005, for a period of at least twenty years or till his death, whichever is earlier. However, the rules allow employees to transfer pension account balance from one eligible pension fund manager to another.

The government had announced pension reforms in 2024 to introduce a contributory pension fund for all government employees, including civil government and armed forces personnel. In a formal announcement in the National Assembly, the government said the contributory pension scheme would apply to all civil employees of the federal government, including civilian employees paid from defence estimates appointed on a regular basis on or after July 1, 2024. A September 2024 notification stated that the scheme would also apply to armed forces personnel appointed on or after July 1, 2025.

While the civilian side of the scheme has been implemented and the government has already set aside about Rs25bn for the scheme as its initial share, the contributory pension scheme for armed forces was deferred for a year to 2026 due to concerns over their peculiar nature of duties requiring detailed review, according to earlier statements by the finance minister and secretary.

Officials said the contributory pension scheme for armed forces personnel, which had been postponed two years ago, had been further delayed owing to internal departmental consultations and challenging security conditions, hindering any move that could be seen demoralising personnel.

The finance ministry notified in October 2025 that federal employees would contribute 10pc of their pensionable pay to qualify for a 12pc contribution from the public exchequer under the newly formalised contributory pension fund scheme. The total contribution rate will thus be 22pc, replacing the traditional pension system for new entrants. The October notification and pension rules superseded an earlier order of August 2024, which had set the government’s contribution at 20pc.

On Aug 20, 2024, the ministry initially announced the introduction of the contributory pension scheme for new entrants to the civil government and armed forces. At that time, employees were to contribute 10pc of their basic pay, while the government was to contribute 20pc.



The contributory pension scheme was introduced on the advice of international lenders, notably the World Bank, to contain the rising pension liabilities, which the government had itself described as a growing fiscal risk. It does not apply to existing employees but aims to slow future growth in pension liabilities. Federal pension expenditure is estimated at Rs1.170tr for FY2026-27, including about Rs860bn for military pensions and about Rs300bn for civil employees. The pension budget had increased from Rs1.055tr in 2025-26.

World.title: Capital Development Authority moves for early start of work on cricket stadium
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Monday held a consultative meeting for the early start of work on the first ever cricket stadium in the capital.

In this regard, the consultant was directed to check at the earliest if construction rates presented by the contractor were reasonable.

As per CDA’s plan, the stadium is going to be constructed near D-12 at the foothills of Margallas in Zone III.

According to the CDA, it will be a replica of Dubai International Stadium with the capacity of 35000 spectators.

Consultant directed to check if rates presented by contractor are reasonable

Sources said the CDA’ member environment Abdullah Khurram Niazi chaired a meeting which was attended by the consultant and contractor and relevant officials of the civic agency.

The CDA has already opened financial bids and a Joint Venture of Habib Construction Service and ZKB-EA has submitted the lowest bid of Rs8.9 billion for the structure work, including a three-kilometre road network. According to PC-I, the estimated cost of the project is Rs11.9 billion. Under the contract, the total covered area is over 600,000 square feet.

Sources said during the meeting, Bills of Quantities (BOQ), scope of the work and other breakdown of the project were discussed and the consultant was directed to complete the process of reasonability of rates so that CDA could issue work orders.

The area where the stadium is going to be constructed is outside of Maraglla Hills National Park, but falls in Zone III, where according to clause 4(3)(b) of the ICT Zoning Regulations 1992, no change in land use is permissible except projects related to recreation, conservation and preservation. Officials said the cricket stadium project falls in the category of recreation.

Asked about the construction of hotels and commercial areas attached to the project, the CDA officials said former chairman Mohammad Ali Randhawa had sent a summary to the federal cabinet seeking permission for hotels and commercial areas.

They said the Prime Minister Office had referred back the summary with some questions and CDA recently resent the same with required information.

Zone III’s status

Officials said the cricket stadium was part of the Olympic Village site of 175 acres, where the CDA had planned several sports facilities including hotels. Out of it, almost 50 acres will be used for the stadium project. The CDA board in its meeting held on November 21, 2025 had decided that a hotel should also be constructed in the area for accommodation of players.

Subsequently, the then chairman CDA moved a summary seeking permission of the federal cabinet for a hotel and a commercial strip at the proposed Olympic Village.

In the year 2022, the CDA board had decided that private areas, including Shah Allah Ditta and other villages of Zone III, should be made part of the nearest Zone I and the area of Bhara Kau should be made part of Zone IV for regulating construction. But the matter could not be taken up by the government.

As per the original master plan, these areas were shown as green. Therefore, if the CDA acquires land in these areas, it will have to leave it for greenery purpose.

“Neither the CDA is acquiring this area nor regulating construction, as a result of which unauthorised construction has been taking place. The issue of this zone should be decided for good,” said an official source.

Meanwhile, the government is showing no interest in resolving the issue of the public in the said unacquired villages of Zone III. However, both the CDA and the government have been showing their intent for construction in Zone III.

Sources said that a few years ago the CDA itself had earmarked land in Zone III for the construction of a special economic zone near Park Road. Last month, the CDA board decided to auction four kanals near the sports complex for motel/hotel project subject to approval of the federal government.

The four kanals is surrendered by Islamabad Club and in a surprising move the CDA wants to auction it for a hotel project, said the sources.

When contacted, CDA spokesperson Shahid Kiani said Zone III and Margalla Hills National Park were different entities.

“As far as cricket stadium project is concerned, being recreational project, it is permissible use in Zone III and approved by CDA board. While, for hotel and commercial components of stadium project, we have not proceeded yet on these two components. Fate of these two components will be decided by federal government, which is a competent forum,” he said.

About a new hotel site in Zone III near sports complex, he said: “Yes, this proposal is under consideration, but no final decision is made yet. There is no issue of construction of motel in said area with approval of federal government as several motels are already existed in said locality, particularly at Rawal Dam Chowk,” he said.

When asked about public suffering, he said: “During the last four years, the issue of public of Zone III was taken up by CDA with federal government. As far as special economic zone in Zone III is concerned, the land for economic zone was taken from NIH and federal government okayed this site, therefore, there is no illegality involved,” he said.
